bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第211卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 211
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 211

sentences.zh: 卷第二百一十一

translations.literal: Volume 211
translations.idiomatic: Volume Two Hundred Eleven

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十七】起閼逢攝提格，盡強圉大荒落，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 27] Beginning in the year cycle Kuimao-Shetige, ending in Qiangyu-Dahuangluo, altogether four years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 27] Spanning the four years from 713 to 716 CE.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬申，制：「選京官有才識者除都督、刺史，都督、刺史有政跡者除京官，使出入常均，永爲恆式。」

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day renshen, an edict: "Select capital officials of talent and insight to appoint as regional governors and prefects; appoint regional governors and prefects with administrative achievements as capital officials, so that movement in and out is regularly balanced, to be an eternal constant rule."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month’s renshen day, an edict declared: "Capital officials of proven ability shall be posted as regional governors and prefects, and governors and prefects with distinguished records shall be recalled to the capital, so that circulation between court and provinces remains even—a rule to hold in perpetuity."

sentences.zh: 己卯，以盧懷慎檢校黃門監。

translations.literal: Day jimao, Lu Huaiqian was made acting Supervisor of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day, Lu Huaiqian was appointed acting Supervisor of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 舊制，雅俗之樂，皆隸太常。

translations.literal: By old regulation, refined and popular music alike were subordinate to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, both court and popular music fell under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 上精曉音律，以太常禮樂之司，不應典倡優雜伎；

translations.literal: The emperor was well versed in pitch and mode, and held that the office charged with ritual and music ought not to preside over singers, actors, and miscellaneous performers;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was himself skilled in music and felt that the ritual-music bureau should not also manage entertainers and variety acts;

sentences.zh: 乃更置左右教坊以教俗樂，命右驍衞將軍范及爲之使。

translations.literal: therefore he newly established the Left and Right Instruction Bureaus to teach popular music, and appointed Right Brave Guard General Fan Ji as their commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: so he created separate Left and Right Instruction Bureaus for popular music and named Fan Ji of the Right Brave Guard as their superintendent.

sentences.zh: 又選樂工數百人，自教法曲於梨園，謂之「皇帝梨園弟子」。

translations.literal: He also selected several hundred musicians and personally taught performance pieces in the Pear Garden, calling them "the emperor’s Pear Garden disciples."
translations.idiomatic: He further chose several hundred musicians and personally taught them new pieces in the Pear Garden, styling them "the emperor’s Pear Garden disciples."

sentences.zh: 又教宮女使習之。

translations.literal: He also had palace women taught to practice them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women were trained in the same repertoire.

sentences.zh: 又選伎女，置宜春院，給賜其家。

translations.literal: He also selected performing women, placed them in the Yichun Courtyard, and granted rewards to their families.
translations.idiomatic: He selected female performers for the Yichun Courtyard and provided stipends for their households.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎張廷珪、酸棗尉袁楚客皆上疏，以爲：「上春秋鼎盛，宜崇經術，邇端士，尚樸素，深以悅鄭聲、好遊獵爲戒。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Tinggui and Suanzao Commandant Yuan Chuke both submitted memorials, stating: "Your Majesty is in the prime of life; you should exalt the classics, draw near upright scholars, esteem simplicity, and take deeply to heart the warning against delighting in Zheng music and fondness for hunting."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinggui, Vice Minister of Rites, and Yuan Chuke, commandant of Suanzao, both memorialized the throne: "Your Majesty stands at the height of his powers; he should honor the classics, keep company with upright men, value plain living, and heed the ancient warning against decadent music and excessive hunting."

sentences.zh: 上雖不能用，欲開言路，鹹嘉賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor, though he could not adopt their advice, wishing to open the path of speech, all praised and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor did not follow their counsel, wishing to encourage frank speech he praised and rewarded them both.

sentences.zh: 中宗以來，貴戚爭營佛寺，奏度人爲僧，兼以偽妄；

translations.literal: Since the time of Emperor Zhongzong, noble kin had vied to establish Buddhist temples, memorializing to ordain people as monks, together with fraud and falsehood;
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Zhongzong’s reign, the imperial clan had competed to build Buddhist temples, petitioning to ordain followers—often by fraudulent means;

sentences.zh: 富戸強丁多削髮以避徭役，所在充滿。

translations.literal: wealthy households and able-bodied men largely shaved their heads to evade corvée labor, and every place was filled with them.
translations.idiomatic: and wealthy families and strong young men took tonsure to escape corvée, until monks crowded every district.

sentences.zh: 姚崇上言：「佛圖澄不能存趙，鳩摩羅什不能存秦，齊襄、梁武，未免禍殃。

translations.literal: Yao Chong submitted: "Fotudeng could not preserve Zhao, Kumarajiva could not preserve Qin; Qi Xiang and Emperor Wu of Liang did not escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong argued: "Fotudeng could not save Later Zhao, Kumarajiva could not save Former Qin, and rulers such as Duke Xiang of Qi and Emperor Wu of Liang still met disaster.

sentences.zh: 但使蒼生安樂，即是佛身；

translations.literal: If only the common people are secure and happy, that itself is the Buddha’s body;
translations.idiomatic: If the people live in peace and contentment, that is the Buddha’s true body;

sentences.zh: 何用妄度奸人，使壞正法！」

translations.literal: why use false ordination of wicked men to ruin the true law!"
translations.idiomatic: why ordain frauds and criminals and thereby corrupt the true teaching!"

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，命有司沙汰天下僧尼，以偽妄還俗者萬二千餘人。

translations.literal: Day bingyin, he ordered the authorities to sift and purge monks and nuns throughout the realm; more than twelve thousand who had been falsely ordained were returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, officials were ordered to review all monks and nuns empire-wide; more than twelve thousand found to have been ordained fraudulently were laicized.

sentences.zh: 初，營州都督治柳城以鎭撫奚、契丹，則天之世，都督趙文翽失政，奚、契丹攻陷之，是後寄治於幽州東漁陽城。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Protectorate-General of Ying Prefecture governed from Liucheng to pacify the Xi and Khitan; in the era of Empress Wu, Protector-General Zhao Wengui lost the government, and the Xi and Khitan attacked and captured it; thereafter administration was lodged at Yuyang east of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Prefecture had once been administered from Liucheng to keep the Xi and Khitan in check, but under Empress Wu its governor Zhao Wengui misruled and the tribes captured the seat; thereafter the protectorate was maintained in exile at Yuyang, east of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 或言：「靺鞨、奚、□大欲降唐，正以唐不建營州，無所依投，爲默啜所侵擾，故且附之；

translations.literal: Someone said: "The Mohe, Xi, and Khitan greatly wish to submit to Tang; it is precisely because Tang has not re-established Ying Prefecture and they have nowhere to rely, and are harassed by Mojilian, that for the time being they attach themselves to him;
translations.idiomatic: Some argued: "The Mohe, Xi, and Khitan would gladly submit to Tang, but with Ying Prefecture unrebuilt they have no refuge and suffer raids from Mojilian, so they cling to him for now;

sentences.zh: 若唐復建營州，則相帥歸化矣。」

translations.literal: if Tang re-establishes Ying Prefecture, then they will lead one another in turning to allegiance."
translations.idiomatic: if Tang restores Ying Prefecture, they will come over in succession."

sentences.zh: 并州長史、和戎大武等軍州節度大使薛訥信之，奏請擊契丹，復置營州；

translations.literal: Bingzhou Chief Secretary and Grand Military Commissioner of Herong-Dawu and other army prefectures Xue Ne believed this, and memorialized requesting to strike the Khitan and restore Ying Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ne, chief secretary of Bingzhou and commissioner over the Hezhong-Dawu circuit, believed this and petitioned to attack the Khitan and re-establish Ying Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 上亦以冷陘之役，欲討契丹。

translations.literal: the emperor also, because of the Lengjing campaign, wished to chastise the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor too, still smarting from the defeat at Lengjing, wished to punish the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 群臣姚崇等多諫。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers Yao Chong and others repeatedly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong and other ministers repeatedly dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以訥同紫微黃門三品，將兵擊契丹，群臣乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Day jiashen, Xue Ne was made co-equal with the Three Departments at Purple Tenuity and Yellow Gate rank and led troops to attack the Khitan; the assembled ministers then did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day, Xue Ne was elevated to third rank in the Purple Tenuity and Yellow Gate and sent to campaign against the Khitan; the court thereafter held its peace.

sentences.zh: 薛王業之舅王仙童，侵暴百姓，御史彈奏；

translations.literal: Prince of Xue Ye’s maternal uncle Wang Xiantong oppressed the common people; censors impeached him;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiantong, uncle of Prince Ye of Xue, had bullied the populace; the censorate brought charges;

sentences.zh: 業爲之請，敕紫微、黃門覆按。

translations.literal: Ye pleaded on his behalf, and an edict ordered the Purple Tenuity and Yellow Gate to re-investigate.
translations.idiomatic: and Prince Ye interceded, prompting an edict for the Purple Tenuity and Yellow Gate to review the case.

sentences.zh: 姚崇、盧懷慎等奏：「仙童罪狀明白，御史所言無所枉，不可縱捨。」

translations.literal: Yao Chong, Lu Huaiqian, and others memorialized: "Xiantong’s crimes are clear; what the censors said is in no way unjust—he cannot be indulged and released."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong and Lu Huaiqian replied: "Xiantong’s guilt is manifest; the censors are not wrong, and he must not go unpunished."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor concurred.

sentences.zh: 由是貴戚束手。

translations.literal: From this the noble kin kept their hands bound.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the imperial kin kept their hands tied.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚寅朔，太史奏太陽應虧不虧。

translations.literal: Second month, first day gengyin, the Grand Astrologer reported that the sun ought to suffer eclipse but did not.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the gengyin new moon, the court astronomer reported that a solar eclipse had been expected but did not occur.

sentences.zh: 姚崇表賀，請書之史冊；

translations.literal: Yao Chong submitted congratulations and requested it be written in the historical records;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong offered congratulations and asked that the event be recorded in the annals;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乙末，突厥可汗默啜遣其子同俄特勒及妹夫火拔頡利發、石阿失畢將兵圍北庭都護府，都護郭虔瓘擊敗之。

translations.literal: Day yiwei, the Türk qaghan Mojilian sent his son Tong’e teili and brothers-in-law Huoba pilifa and Shi Ashibi to lead troops and besiege the Protectorate of Beiting; Protector-General Guo Qianzhen defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day, the Türk qaghan Mojilian sent his son Tong’e, his brothers-in-law Huoba and Shi Ashibi, and an army to besiege Beiting; Protector-General Guo Qianzhen routed them.

sentences.zh: 同俄單騎逼城下，虔瓘伏壯士於道側，突起斬之。

translations.literal: Tong’e alone on horseback pressed to below the wall; Qianzhen hid strong men beside the road and suddenly rose up and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong’e rode alone to the walls; Qianzhen had braves lie in ambush along the road and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 突厥請悉軍中資糧以贖同俄，聞其已死，慟哭而去。

translations.literal: The Türks requested all the army’s provisions and grain to ransom Tong’e; hearing he was already dead, they wailed and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks offered all their army’s stores to ransom Tong’e; learning he was dead, they wept and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丁未，敕：「自今所在毋得創建佛寺；

translations.literal: Day dingwei, an edict: "From now on, nowhere may newly create Buddhist temples;
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day, an edict declared: "Henceforth no new Buddhist temples may be built anywhere;

sentences.zh: 舊寺頹壞應葺者，詣有司陳牒檢視，然後聽之。」

translations.literal: where old temples are ruined and should be repaired, one must go to the authorities with a petition for inspection, and only then is it permitted."
translations.idiomatic: repairs to existing temples must be reported to the authorities for inspection before work may proceed."

sentences.zh: 閏月，以鴻臚少卿、朔方軍副大總管王晙兼安北大都護、朔方道行軍大總管，令豐安、定遠、三受降城及旁側諸軍皆受晙節度。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, Wang Jun, Vice Minister of the Court for Dependencies and deputy grand general of the Shuofang Army, was also made Protector-General of Anding North and campaigning grand general of the Shuofang circuit, ordering Feng’an, Dingyuan, the three Accept-the-Surrender cities, and neighboring armies all to accept Jun’s command.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Wang Jun, vice minister of the Court for Dependencies and deputy commander of Shuofang, was also named Protector-General of Anding North and grand campaign commander on the Shuofang circuit, with Feng’an, Dingyuan, the three surrender cities, and adjacent garrisons all placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 徙大都護府於中受降城，置兵屯田。

translations.literal: The great protectorate headquarters was moved to the central Accept-the-Surrender city, and troops were stationed for garrison agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: The protectorate seat was moved to the central surrender city and troops were settled on frontier farms.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，復置十道按察使，以益州長史陸象先等爲之。

translations.literal: Day dingmao, the ten-circuit investigation commissioners were restored, with Yizhou Chief Secretary Lu Xiangxian and others appointed.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, the ten regional inspection commissioners were reinstated, with Lu Xiangxian of Yizhou among them.

sentences.zh: 上思徐有功用法平直，乙亥，以其子大理司直惀爲恭陵令。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled Xu Yougong’s straightforward use of law; day yihai, his son Xu Lun, rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review, was made magistrate of Gongling.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering Xu Yougong’s impartial administration of justice, on the yihai day the emperor appointed his son Xu Lun, a judicial reviewer, magistrate of Gongling.

sentences.zh: 竇孝諶之子光祿卿豳公希瑊等，請以己官爵讓惀以報其德，由是惀累遷申王府司馬。

translations.literal: Dou Xiaochen’s son, Director of the Imperial Household and Duke of Bin Xi Chen and others, requested to yield their own offices and titles to Lun in repayment of his virtue; thereby Lun was repeatedly promoted to secretary of the Prince of Shen’s establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chen, Director of the Imperial Household and son of Dou Xiaochen, and others offered their own ranks to Xu Lun in gratitude; Lun was thereafter promoted to secretary of the Prince of Shen’s household.

sentences.zh: 丙子，申王成義請以其府錄事閻楚珪爲其府參軍，上許之。

translations.literal: Day bingzi, the Prince of Shen Cheng Yi requested that his establishment recorder Yan Chugui be made his establishment adjutant; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day, Prince Cheng Yi of Shen asked to appoint his recorder Yan Chugui as a staff adjutant, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 姚崇、盧懷慎上言：「先嘗得旨，雲王公、駙馬有所奏請，非墨敕皆勿行。

translations.literal: Yao Chong and Lu Huaiqian submitted: "We previously received an order stating that when princes and imperial sons-in-law make requests, unless there is an ink edict none are to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong and Lu Huaiqian objected: "Your Majesty once ruled that princes and imperial sons-in-law might petition only by personal edict—otherwise requests were not to be honored.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以量材授官，當歸有司；

translations.literal: We humbly consider that assigning offices according to talent ought to belong to the proper offices;
translations.idiomatic: Appointments should be made by the proper agencies according to merit;

sentences.zh: 若緣親故之恩，得以官爵爲惠，踵習近事，實紊紀綱。」

translations.literal: if by reason of kinship favor one may use office and rank as bounty, following recent practice, this truly disorders the statutes and guidelines."
translations.idiomatic: to grant offices as favors through kinship, as has lately been done, would only disorder the bureaucracy."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter thereupon lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 由是請謁不行。

translations.literal: From this, requests and audiences did not go through.
translations.idiomatic: Patronage petitions thereafter failed.

sentences.zh: 突厥石阿失畢既失同俄，不敢歸，癸未，與其妻來奔；

translations.literal: The Türk Shi Ashibi, having lost Tong’e, did not dare return; day guimao, he and his wife came to defect;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ashibi of the Türks, unable to return after Tong’e’s death, defected with his wife on the guimao day;

sentences.zh: 以爲右衞大將軍，封燕北郡王，命其妻曰金山公主。

translations.literal: he was made General of the Right Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Yanbei commandery, and his wife was titled Princess Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: he was made a general of the Right Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Yanbei, and his wife was named Princess Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 或告太子少保劉幽求、太子詹事鐘紹京有怨望語，下紫微省按問，幽求等不服。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent Liu Youqiu and Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent Zhong Shaojing had resentful words; the case was sent down to the Purple Tenuity office for interrogation, and Youqiu and others did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu, junior tutor to the crown prince, and Zhong Shaojing, household administrator to the heir, were accused of disloyal remarks; the Purple Tenuity office investigated, and they denied the charges.

sentences.zh: 姚崇、盧懷慎、薛訥言於上曰：「幽求等皆功臣，乍就閒職，微有沮喪，人情或然。

translations.literal: Yao Chong, Lu Huaiqian, and Xue Ne said to the emperor: "Youqiu and the others are all meritorious ministers; suddenly placed in idle posts, they are slightly dejected—such human feeling may occur.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong, Lu Huaiqian, and Xue Ne urged: "Youqiu and the rest are founding ministers recently given idle posts; a trace of disappointment would be only human.

sentences.zh: 功業既大，榮寵亦深，一朝下獄，慮驚遠聽。」

translations.literal: Their achievements are already great and their honor deep; in one morning to cast them into prison—we fear alarming distant listeners."
translations.idiomatic: Their services are great and their honors many; to imprison them overnight would alarm the empire."

sentences.zh: 戊子，貶幽求爲睦州刺史，紹京爲果州刺史，紫微侍郎王琚行邊軍未還，亦坐幽求黨貶澤州刺史。

translations.literal: Day wuzi, Youqiu was demoted to prefect of Mu, Shaojing to prefect of Guo; Purple Tenuity Vice Minister Wang Ju, on border duty and not yet returned, was also implicated as Youqiu’s partisan and demoted to prefect of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day, Youqiu was demoted to prefect of Mu and Shaojing to prefect of Guo; Wang Ju of the Purple Tenuity, away on frontier duty, was implicated as an associate and demoted to prefect of Ze.

sentences.zh: 敕：「涪州刺史周利貞等十三人，皆天後時酷吏，比周興等情狀差輕，宜放歸草澤，終身勿齒。」

translations.literal: An edict: "Fu Prefecture Prefect Zhou Lizhen and thirteen others were all cruel officials of Empress Wu’s time; compared with Zhou Xing and others their circumstances are somewhat lighter—they should be released to the wilds and never ranked among officials for life."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "Zhou Lizhen of Fu Prefecture and twelve others, cruel officials from Empress Wu’s reign, though less guilty than men like Zhou Xing, are to be released to private life and barred from office forever."

sentences.zh: 西突厥十姓酋長都擔叛。

translations.literal: The chieftain of the Western Türk ten surnames, Dudan, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Dudan, chief of the Western Türk ten tribes, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 三月，己亥，磧西節度使阿史那獻克碎葉等鎭，擒斬都擔，降其部落二萬餘帳。

translations.literal: Third month, day jihai, Hexi frontier commissioner Ashina Xian captured Suyab and other garrisons, seized and executed Dudan, and received the surrender of more than twenty thousand tents of his tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the jihai day, Ashina Xian, commissioner of the Western Regions, took Suyab and neighboring posts, killed Dudan, and accepted the submission of more than twenty thousand tents.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞姜晦以宗楚客等改中宗遺詔，青州刺史韋安石、太子賓客韋嗣立、刑部尚書趙彥昭、特進致仕李嶠，於時同爲宰相，不能匡正，令監察御史郭震彈之；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Jiang Hui, because Zong Chuke and others had altered Emperor Zhongzong’s death edict, [charged that] Qingzhou Prefect Wei Anshi, Household Guest of the Heir Apparent Wei Silizhi, Minister of Justice Zhao Yanzhao, and retired Grand Mentor Li Qiao had at the time all been chancellors together and could not correct it; he ordered investigating censor Guo Zhen to impeach them;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Jiang Hui, citing Zong Chuke’s alteration of Emperor Zhongzong’s will, had investigating censor Guo Zhen impeach Wei Anshi, former chancellor and now prefect of Qingzhou, Wei Silizhi, Zhao Yanzhao, and the retired Li Qiao for failing to stop it;

sentences.zh: 且言彥昭拜巫趙氏爲姑，蒙婦人服，與妻乘車詣其家。

translations.literal: and further stated that Yanzhao had worshipped the shamaness Lady Zhao as his aunt, donned women’s dress, and with his wife rode in a carriage to her house.
translations.idiomatic: and further accused Zhao Yanzhao of honoring a shamaness as his aunt, wearing women’s dress, and visiting her home with his wife in a carriage.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，貶安石爲沔州別駕，嗣立爲岳州別駕，彥昭爲袁州別駕，嶠爲滁州別駕。

translations.literal: Day jiachen, Anshi was demoted to vice-prefect of Mian, Silizhi to vice-prefect of Yue, Yanzhao to vice-prefect of Yuan, and Qiao to vice-prefect of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day, Anshi was demoted to vice-prefect of Mian, Silizhi of Yue, Yanzhao of Yuan, and Qiao of Chu.

sentences.zh: 安石至沔州，晦又奏安石嘗檢校定陵，盜隱官物，下州征贓。

translations.literal: When Anshi reached Mian Prefecture, Hui again memorialized that Anshi had once served as acting supervisor of Dingling and had concealed official goods; the prefecture was ordered to collect the stolen goods.
translations.idiomatic: After Anshi reached Mian, Hui charged that he had embezzled goods while supervising Emperor Zhongzong’s tomb and ordered the prefecture to recover them.

sentences.zh: 安石歎曰：「此只應須我死耳。」

translations.literal: Anshi sighed: "This can only mean they want me dead."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi sighed: "They will not be satisfied until I am dead."

sentences.zh: 憤恚而卒。

translations.literal: He died in anger and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He died of outrage and grief.

sentences.zh: 晦，皎之弟也。

translations.literal: Hui was the younger brother of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was the younger brother of Jiang Jiao.

sentences.zh: 毀天樞，發匠熔其銅鐵，歷月不盡。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Pivot was destroyed; craftsmen were sent to smelt its bronze and iron, and for months it was not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Pivot monument was torn down; smiths melted its bronze and iron for months without finishing.

sentences.zh: 先是，韋後亦於天街作石台，高數丈，以頌功德，至是並毀之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Empress Wei had also made a stone platform on the Imperial Avenue, several zhang high, to praise merit and virtue; at this time it too was destroyed together.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei had earlier built a stone platform several zhang high on the Imperial Avenue to glorify her reign; it too was demolished.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛巳，突厥可汗默啜復遣使求昏，自稱「乾和永清太駙馬、天上得果報天男、突厥聖天骨咄祿可汗」。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinsi, the Türk qaghan Mojilian again sent envoys seeking marriage, styling himself "Great Imperial Son-in-Law of Qianhe and Yongqing, Heaven-receiving Fruit-rewarding Heaven-Man, Türk Sacred Heaven Ashina Qaghan."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fourth month’s xinsi day, Mojilian again sought a marriage alliance, styling himself "Great Son-in-Law of Qianhe and Yongqing, Heaven’s Blessed Son of Heaven, Sacred Türk Qaghan of the Ashina."

sentences.zh: 五月，己丑，以歲饑，悉罷員外、試、檢校官，自今非戰功及別敕，毋得注擬。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day jichou, because of famine in the year, all supernumerary, probationary, and acting officials were entirely dismissed; from now on, except for military merit and special edicts, none may be nominated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the jichou day, famine prompted the abolition of all supernumerary, probationary, and acting appointments; hereafter only men with battlefield merit or special edicts might receive office.

sentences.zh: 己酉，吐蕃相坌達延遺宰相書，請先遣解琬至河源正二國封疆，然後結盟。

translations.literal: Day jiyou, the Tibetan minister Ben Dazhi sent a letter to the chancellor, requesting that Jie Wan first be sent to Heyuan to rectify the two states’ borders, and only then conclude alliance.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day, the Tibetan minister Ben Dazhi wrote the Tang chancellor asking that Jie Wan be sent first to Heyuan to fix the border before any alliance was concluded.

sentences.zh: 琬嘗爲朔方大總管，故吐蕃請之。

translations.literal: Wan had once been grand general of Shuofang; therefore the Tibetans requested him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans had asked for Wan because he had once commanded Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 前此琬以金紫光祿大夫致仕，復召拜左散騎常侍而遣之。

translations.literal: Before this Wan had retired as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; he was again summoned and appointed Left Regular Attendant and sent.
translations.idiomatic: Wan had retired as a grand master of the court; he was now recalled as Left Regular Attendant and dispatched.

sentences.zh: 又命宰相復坌達延書，招懷之。

translations.literal: The chancellor was also ordered to reply to Ben Dazhi’s letter and win him over.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor was also instructed to answer Ben Dazhi’s letter in a conciliatory tone.

sentences.zh: 琬上言：「吐蕃必陰懷叛計，請預屯兵十萬於秦、渭等州以備之。」

translations.literal: Wan submitted: "Tibet surely harbors secret plans of rebellion; I request beforehand stationing one hundred thousand troops in Qin, Wei, and other prefectures to guard against it."
translations.idiomatic: Wan warned: "Tibet surely plots treachery; I ask that a hundred thousand men be stationed in advance at Qin, Wei, and neighboring prefectures."

sentences.zh: 黃門監魏知古，本起小吏，因姚崇引薦，以至同爲相。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Supervisor Wei Zhigu had originally risen from minor clerk; through Yao Chong’s recommendation he reached serving together as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhigu, Supervisor of the Yellow Gate, had begun as a petty clerk and reached the chancellorship through Yao Chong’s patronage.

sentences.zh: 崇意輕之，請知古攝吏部尚書、知東都選事，遣吏部尚書宋璟於門下過官；

translations.literal: Chong looked down on him, requested that Zhigu act as Minister of Personnel and oversee Eastern Capital selection, and sent Minister of Personnel Song Jing to pass on appointments at the Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Chong slighted him, had him made acting Minister of Personnel in charge of Luoyang appointments, and sent Song Jing to approve nominations at court;

sentences.zh: 知古銜之。

translations.literal: Zhigu harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu resented the humiliation.

sentences.zh: 崇二子分司東都，恃其父有德於知古，頗招權請托；

translations.literal: Chong’s two sons served in the Eastern Capital branch office; relying on their father’s favor owed by Zhigu, they rather gathered power and requests;
translations.idiomatic: Chong’s two sons held posts in Luoyang and, believing Zhigu owed their father a debt, traded on his influence;

sentences.zh: 知古歸，悉以聞。

translations.literal: when Zhigu returned to court, he reported all of it.
translations.idiomatic: on returning to the capital, Zhigu reported everything to the throne.

sentences.zh: 他日，上從容問崇：「卿子才性何如？

translations.literal: Another day, the emperor casually asked Chong: "What are your sons’ talents and natures?
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor casually asked Chong: "What are your sons like?

sentences.zh: 今何官也？」

translations.literal: What offices do they hold now?"
translations.idiomatic: What posts do they hold?"

sentences.zh: 崇揣知上意，對曰：「臣有三子，兩在東都，爲人多欲而不謹，是必以事幹魏知古，臣未及問之耳。」

translations.literal: Chong guessed the emperor’s intent and replied: "Your servant has three sons; two are in the Eastern Capital. They are men of many desires and not careful—they must surely have matters involving Wei Zhigu; your servant has not yet had time to ask."
translations.idiomatic: Chong guessed the emperor’s purpose and answered: "I have three sons; two are in Luoyang. They are greedy and careless and must have importuned Wei Zhigu—I have not yet questioned them."

sentences.zh: 上始以崇必爲其子隱，及聞崇奏，喜問：「卿安從知之？」

translations.literal: The emperor at first thought Chong would certainly conceal his sons; hearing Chong’s report, he asked with pleasure: "How did you know?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had expected Chong to shield his sons; delighted, he asked: "How did you know?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「知古微時，臣卵而翼之。

translations.literal: He replied: "When Zhigu was humble, your servant nourished him as an egg and winged him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied: "When Zhigu was obscure, I sheltered him as a chick under my wing.

sentences.zh: 臣子愚，以爲知古必德臣，容其爲非，故敢干之耳。」

translations.literal: Your servant’s sons are foolish; they thought Zhigu must feel gratitude to your servant and would tolerate their wrongdoing, so they dared to importune him."
translations.idiomatic: My foolish sons assumed he would indulge them out of gratitude, and so they dared to approach him."

sentences.zh: 上於是以崇爲無私，而薄知古負崇，欲斥之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon regarded Chong as unselfish, but looked lightly on Zhigu for being ungrateful to Chong and wished to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then judged Chong impartial but blamed Zhigu for ingratitude and wished to remove him.

sentences.zh: 崇固請曰：「臣子無狀，撓陛下法，陛下赦其罪，已幸矣；

translations.literal: Chong firmly pleaded: "Your servant’s sons are ill-behaved and disturbed Your Majesty’s law; Your Majesty pardoned their crime—that was already fortunate;
translations.idiomatic: Chong protested: "My sons have shamed me and violated your law; your pardon was mercy enough;

sentences.zh: 苟因臣逐知古，天下必以陛下爲私於臣，累聖政矣。」

translations.literal: if because of your servant you drive out Zhigu, the realm will surely think Your Majesty partial to your servant—this would harm sagely government."
translations.idiomatic: if you dismiss Zhigu on my account, the realm will think you favor me over justice and your rule will suffer."

sentences.zh: 上久乃許之。

translations.literal: After long [consideration] the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: After long hesitation the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，知古罷爲工部尚書。

translations.literal: Day xinhai, Zhigu was removed and made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day, Zhigu was demoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 宋王成器，申王成義，上之兄也；

translations.literal: Prince of Song Chengqi and Prince of Shen Chengyi were the emperor’s elder brothers;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chengqi of Song and Prince Chengyi of Shen were the emperor’s elder brothers;

sentences.zh: 岐王范，薛王業，上之弟也；

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Fan and Prince of Xue Ye were the emperor’s younger brothers;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fan of Qi and Prince Ye of Xue were his younger brothers;

sentences.zh: 豳王守禮，上之從兄也。

translations.literal: Prince of Bin Shouli was the emperor’s cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shouli of Bin was his cousin.

sentences.zh: 上素友愛，近世帝王莫能及。

translations.literal: The emperor had always been friendly and loving; recent emperors could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s affection for them exceeded that of any recent sovereign.

sentences.zh: 初即位，爲長枕大被，與兄弟同寢。

translations.literal: When he first took the throne, he made a long pillow and large quilt and slept together with his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign he had a long pillow and wide quilt made so that he might sleep in the same bed with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 諸王每旦朝於側門，退則相從宴飲、鬥雞、擊球，或獵於近郊，游賞別墅，中使存問相望於道。

translations.literal: Every morning the princes attended court at the side gate; when they withdrew they followed one another in feasting and drinking, cockfighting, and ball games, or hunted in the near suburbs and toured villa estates, palace envoys sending inquiries visible one after another along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning the princes attended court at the side gate; after dismissing they kept company in feasting, cockfighting, and polo, or hunted in the nearby countryside and visited country villas, while palace envoys bearing inquiries lined the roads in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 上聽朝罷，多從諸王游，在禁中，拜跪如家人禮，飲食起居，相與同之。

translations.literal: When the emperor finished hearing court, he often went about with the princes; within the palace precincts they bowed and knelt with the rites of family members, and in eating, drinking, rising, and resting they shared the same arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: When court adjourned, the emperor often kept the princes' company; within the palace they bowed and knelt as family members might, sharing meals, quarters, and daily routines.

sentences.zh: 於殿中設五幄，與諸王更處其中，謂之五王帳。

translations.literal: Five tent-canopies were set up in the hall, and the emperor and the princes took turns dwelling within them—this was called the Five Princes' Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Five canopied alcoves were erected in the hall where the emperor and princes took turns lodging—this they called the Pavilion of the Five Princes.

sentences.zh: 或講論賦詩，間以飲酒、博弈、遊獵，或自執絲竹；

translations.literal: Sometimes they discoursed on literature and composed poetry, interspersed with drinking wine, gambling, and hunting, or the emperor himself took up string and wind instruments;
translations.idiomatic: They might discuss poetry and compose verses, interluding with wine, games of chance, and hunts—or the emperor himself would take up the lute and flute;

sentences.zh: 成器善笛，范善琵琶，與上共奏之。

translations.literal: Chengqi was skilled at the flute, Fan at the pipa, and together with the emperor they performed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqi excelled at the flute and Fan at the pipa; together they played with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 諸王或有疾，上爲之終日不食，終夜不寢。

translations.literal: When any of the princes fell ill, the emperor would go all day without eating and all night without sleeping on their account.
translations.idiomatic: If any prince fell ill, the emperor would neither eat all day nor sleep all night for worry.

sentences.zh: 業嘗疾，上方臨朝，須臾之間，使者十返。

translations.literal: Ye once fell ill; the emperor was just holding court when, within the space of a moment, messengers came and went ten times.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye once fell ill, the emperor was holding court; within minutes messengers had shuttled back and forth ten times.

sentences.zh: 上親爲業煮藥，回飆吹火，誤爇上須，左右驚救之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally boiled medicine for Ye; a whirlwind blew the flame and accidentally singed the emperor's beard, and those nearby cried out in alarm and rushed to save him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally brewed medicine for Ye; a gust of wind fanned the flame and scorched his beard, and attendants cried out and rushed to his aid.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「但使王飲此藥而愈，須何足惜！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So long as the prince drinks this medicine and recovers, what is a beard not worth sparing!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If only the prince drinks this and recovers—what is a beard worth sparing!"

sentences.zh: 成器尤恭慎，未嘗議及時政，與人交結；

translations.literal: Chengqi was especially respectful and cautious, never once discussing current affairs or forming ties with people;
translations.idiomatic: Chengqi was especially deferential and circumspect; he never discussed state affairs or cultivated political alliances;

sentences.zh: 上愈信重之，故讒間之言無自而入。

translations.literal: The emperor trusted and valued him all the more, so words of slander and alienation had no way to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted him all the more, and slander had no opening to reach him.

sentences.zh: 然專以衣食聲色畜養娛樂之，不任以職事。

translations.literal: Yet he devoted himself solely to providing them with clothing, food, music, and women for their nurture and amusement, and did not assign them duties of office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept them only in fine food, dress, music, and pleasure—entertainment without office or responsibility.

sentences.zh: 群臣以成器等地逼，請循故事出刺外州。

translations.literal: The ministers, because Chengqi and the others' proximity to the capital was pressing, requested that according to precedent they be sent out to serve as regional governors in outer provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers, alarmed that Chengqi and the others' estates pressed too close to the capital, asked that by precedent they be posted to govern distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁巳，以宋王成器兼岐州刺史，申王成義兼幽州刺史，幽王守禮兼虢州刺史，令到官但領大綱，自餘州務，皆委上佐主之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day disi, Prince of Song Chengqi was additionally appointed Prefect of Qi Prefecture, Prince of Shen Chengyi additionally Prefect of You Prefecture, Prince of You Shouli additionally Prefect of Guo Prefecture—they were ordered that upon reaching office they need only oversee the broad outlines, while all remaining prefectural affairs were to be entrusted to chief assistants to manage.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the disi day, Prince of Song Chengqi was made concurrent Prefect of Qi, Prince of Shen Chengyi of You, and Prince of You Shouli of Guo; they were told to grasp only the broad outlines once in office, leaving all other prefectural business to their chief deputies.

sentences.zh: 是後諸王爲都護、都督、刺史者並准此。

translations.literal: Thereafter princes who served as protectorate commanders, area commanders, or prefects all followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all princes appointed protectorate commanders, area commanders, or prefects followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，吐蕃使其宰相尚欽藏來獻盟書。

translations.literal: Day bingyin, Tibet sent its chancellor Shang Qinzang to present the alliance document.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, Tibet dispatched its chancellor Shang Qinzang to present the treaty document.

sentences.zh: 上以風俗奢靡，秋，七月，乙未，制：「乘輿服御、金銀器玩，宜令有司銷毀，以供軍國之用；

translations.literal: Because customs were extravagant and wasteful, in autumn, seventh month, day yiwei, an edict: "Imperial carriages, clothing, gold and silver vessels and curios—all these should be ordered destroyed by the authorities to supply military and state needs;
translations.idiomatic: Finding the customs extravagantly wasteful, in the seventh month of autumn, on the yiwei day, an edict declared: "Imperial carriages, vestments, and gold and silver vessels and ornaments shall be melted down by the authorities for military and state use;

sentences.zh: 其珠玉、錦繡，焚於殿前；

translations.literal: pearls, jade, and brocades are to be burned before the hall;
translations.idiomatic: pearls, jade, and brocades shall be burned before the palace hall;

sentences.zh: 后妃以下，皆毋得服珠玉錦繡。」

translations.literal: empresses and consorts downward—all may not wear pearls, jade, or brocades."
translations.idiomatic: from empresses and consorts downward, none may wear pearls, jade, or brocade."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，敕：「百官所服帶及酒器、馬銜、鐙，三品以上，聽飾以玉，四品以金，五品以銀，自餘皆禁之；

translations.literal: Day wuxu, an edict: "The belts worn by officials, as well as wine vessels, horse bits, and stirrups—those of third rank and above may ornament with jade, fourth rank with gold, fifth rank with silver, all others are forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day, an edict ordered: "Officials' belts, wine vessels, horse bits, and stirrups—third rank and above may ornament with jade, fourth with gold, fifth with silver; all others are forbidden;

sentences.zh: 婦人服飾從其夫、子。

translations.literal: women's dress and ornaments follow their husbands and sons.
translations.idiomatic: women's dress and ornaments shall follow their husbands' and sons' ranks.

sentences.zh: 其舊成錦繡，聽染爲皁。

translations.literal: Existing finished brocades may be dyed black.
translations.idiomatic: Existing brocades may be dyed black.

sentences.zh: 自今天下更毋得採珠玉，織錦繡等物，違者杖一百，工人減一等。」

translations.literal: From today throughout the realm none may further gather pearls and jade or weave brocades and the like; violators receive one hundred strokes of the staff, craftsmen reduced one degree in punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth no one in the realm may gather pearls and jade or weave brocades; violators receive one hundred strokes, artisans one degree less."

sentences.zh: 罷兩京織錦坊。

translations.literal: The brocade-weaving offices of the two capitals were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The brocade workshops of the two capitals were abolished.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：明皇之始欲爲治，能自刻厲節儉如此，晩節猶以奢敗。

translations.literal: Sima Guang remarks: At the beginning Emperor Ming wished to govern well and was able to restrain himself and be frugal to this degree, yet in his later years he still ruined himself through extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: At the outset Emperor Ming meant to govern well and could restrain himself to such frugality—yet even so his later years were undone by extravagance.

sentences.zh: 甚哉奢靡之易以溺人也！

translations.literal: How greatly does extravagance easily drown a person!
translations.idiomatic: How easily does extravagance drown a man!

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「靡不有初，鮮克有終。」

translations.literal: The Odes says: "There is none who does not have a beginning, but few can have an end."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says: "All things have a beginning, but few see an end."

sentences.zh: 可不慎哉！

translations.literal: Can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Can one not take heed!

sentences.zh: 薛訥與左臨門衞將軍杜賓客、定州刺史崔宣道等將兵六萬出檀州擊契丹。

translations.literal: Xue Ne, together with Left Commander of the Left Gate Guard Du Binke, Prefect of Dingzhou Cui Xuandao, and others led sixty thousand troops out from Tanzhou to attack the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ne, with Left Gate Guard General Du Binke, Prefect of Dingzhou Cui Xuandao, and others, led sixty thousand men from Tanzhou against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 賓客以爲「士卒盛夏負戈甲，繼資糧，深入寇境，難以成功。」

translations.literal: Binke held that "in midsummer the soldiers bear armor and weapons and carry provisions, penetrating deep into enemy territory—it will be hard to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Binke argued that "in midsummer, troops burdened with armor and supplies, pushing deep into enemy country, can scarcely succeed."

sentences.zh: 訥曰：「盛夏草肥，羔犢孳息，因糧於敵，正得天時，一舉滅虜，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Ne said: "In midsummer the grass is lush; lambs and calves multiply. Living off the enemy's grain—we have heaven's season on our side. Wiping out the barbarians in one stroke—we must not miss this."
translations.idiomatic: Ne replied: "In midsummer the grass is rich and flocks breed; we can live off the enemy's stores—heaven favors us. To crush the foe in one blow—we must not let this pass."

sentences.zh: 行至灤水山峽中，契丹伏兵遮其前後，從山上擊之。

translations.literal: When they reached the mountain defiles along the Luan River, Khitan ambush troops blocked them front and rear and struck them from the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered the mountain passes of the Luan River, Khitan ambushers blocked them fore and aft and struck from the heights.

sentences.zh: 唐兵大敗，死者什八九。

translations.literal: Tang troops suffered a great defeat; eight or nine out of ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Tang forces were routed; eight or nine in ten perished.

sentences.zh: 訥與數十騎突圍得免，虜中嗤之，謂之「薛婆。」

translations.literal: Ne broke out of encirclement with several dozen horsemen and escaped; among the barbarians they mocked him, calling him "Old Woman Xue."
translations.idiomatic: Ne broke through with a few dozen horsemen and escaped; the enemy mocked him as "Old Woman Xue."

sentences.zh: 崔宣道將後軍，聞訥敗，亦走。

translations.literal: Cui Xuandao commanded the rear army; hearing of Ne's defeat, he fled as well.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuandao, commanding the rear guard, fled too on hearing of Ne's defeat.

sentences.zh: 訥歸罪於宣道及胡將李思敬等八人，制悉斬之於幽州。

translations.literal: Ne assigned blame to Xuandao and the foreign general Li Sijing and seven others; by edict all were beheaded at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ne blamed Xuandao and the foreign general Li Sijing and seven others; by edict all eight were executed at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚子，敕免訥死，削除其官爵；

translations.literal: Day gengzi, an edict spared Ne from death but stripped his office and titles;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day, an edict spared Ne's life but stripped his rank and titles;

sentences.zh: 獨赦杜賓客之罪。

translations.literal: Du Binke alone was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Du Binke alone was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以北庭都護郭虔瓘爲涼州刺史、河西諸軍州節度使。

translations.literal: Day renyin, Protector-General of Beiting Guo Qianzhen was made Prefect of Liangzhou and military commissioner of the army prefectures of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day, Beiting Protector-General Guo Qianzhen was appointed Prefect of Liangzhou and military commissioner of the Hexi army prefectures.

sentences.zh: 果州刺史鐘紹京心怨望，數上疏妄陳休咎；

translations.literal: Prefect of Guozhou Zhong Shaojing harbored resentment in his heart and repeatedly submitted memorials recklessly stating auspicious and inauspicious portents;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shaojing, Prefect of Guo, nursed grievances and repeatedly memorialized with reckless talk of omens and portents;

sentences.zh: 乙巳，貶溱州刺史。

translations.literal: Day yisi, he was demoted to Prefect of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day he was demoted to Prefect of Qin.

sentences.zh: 丁未，房州刺史襄王重茂薨。

translations.literal: Day dingwei, Prince of Xiang Chongmao, Prefect of Fang Prefecture, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day, Prince of Xiang Chongmao, Prefect of Fang, died.

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日，追謚曰殤皇帝。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously ennobled Emperor Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously titled Emperor Shang.

sentences.zh: 戊申，禁百官家毋得與僧、尼、道士往還。

translations.literal: Day wushen, it was forbidden for officials' households to have dealings with monks, nuns, or Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, officials' households were forbidden to associate with monks, nuns, or Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 壬子，禁人間鑄佛、寫經。

translations.literal: Day renzi, the people were forbidden to cast Buddha images or copy sutras.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day, the casting of Buddha images and copying of sutras among the people was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 宋王成器等請獻興慶坊宅爲離宮；

translations.literal: Prince of Song Chengqi and the others requested to present their Xingqing Ward residences as detached palaces;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Song Chengqi and the others offered their Xingqing Ward mansions as detached palaces;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，制許之，始作興慶宮，仍各賜成器等宅，環於宮側。

translations.literal: Day jiayin, by edict this was permitted; construction of Xingqing Palace began, and each of Chengqi and the others was still granted a residence encircling the palace on its flanks.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day the request was granted; Xingqing Palace was begun, and new residences for Chengqi and the others were granted ringing the palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 又於宮西南置樓，題其西曰「花萼相輝之樓」，南曰「勤政務本之樓」。

translations.literal: Towers were also erected southwest of the palace; the western one was inscribed "Tower of Flower and Calyx Mutual Splendor," the southern one "Tower of Diligent Governance and Rooted in Essentials."
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the palace towers were built; the western tower was named "Tower of Mutual Splendor among Flower and Calyx," the southern "Tower of Diligent Governance and Rooted in Fundamentals."

sentences.zh: 上或登樓，聞王奏樂，則召升樓同宴，或幸其所居盡歡，賞賚優渥。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended a tower and heard a prince performing music, he would summon him up to feast together; sometimes he visited their dwellings and caroused to the full, bestowing generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor climbed a tower and heard a prince playing music, he would summon him to feast together; sometimes he visited their homes and revelled to the full, lavishing rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以岐王范兼絳州刺史，薛王業兼同州刺史。

translations.literal: Day yimao, Prince of Qi Fan was additionally made Prefect of Jiang Prefecture, Prince of Xue Ye additionally Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day, Prince of Qi Fan was made concurrent Prefect of Jiang, and Prince of Xue Ye of Tong.

sentences.zh: 仍敕宋王以下每季二人入朝，週而復始。

translations.literal: It was further decreed that from the Prince of Song downward, two each season would enter court, rotating in cycle.
translations.idiomatic: It was further decreed that from the Prince of Song downward, two princes each season would attend court, rotating in turn.

sentences.zh: 民間訛言上采擇女子以充掖庭。

translations.literal: Among the people a false rumor spread that the emperor was selecting women to fill the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: A rumor spread among the people that the emperor was selecting girls for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，八月，乙丑，令有司具車牛於崇明門，自選後宮無用者載還其家；

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, in the eighth month, day yichou, he ordered the authorities to prepare carts and oxen at Chongming Gate and himself selected useless women from the rear palace to be sent home in them;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, in the eighth month on the yichou day he had carts and oxen readied at Chongming Gate and personally chose superfluous women from the inner palace to be sent home;

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「燕寢之內，尚令罷遣；

translations.literal: an edict stated: "Even within the inner palace chambers, I have ordered dismissals;
translations.idiomatic: an edict read: "Even within the inner chambers I have ordered dismissals;

sentences.zh: 閭閻之間，足可知悉。」

translations.literal: among the lanes and wards of the realm, this should be fully known."
translations.idiomatic: among the lanes and wards, let this be fully understood."

sentences.zh: 乙亥，吐蕃將坌達延、乞力徐帥眾十萬寇臨洮，軍蘭州，至於渭源，掠取牧馬。

translations.literal: Day yihai, Tibetan generals Bendayan and Qili Xu led a force of one hundred thousand to raid Lin-tao, encamped at Lanzhou, reached as far as Wei River source, and plundered pasture horses.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day, Tibetan generals Bendayan and Qili Xu led one hundred thousand men to raid Lintao, camp at Lanzhou, reach Weiyuan, and seize pasture horses.

sentences.zh: 命薛訥白衣攝左羽林將軍，爲隴右防禦使。

translations.literal: Xue Ne was ordered, in plain clothes, to act as General of the Left Feathered Forest and serve as defense commissioner of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ne, though in plain dress, was ordered to act as General of the Left Feathered Forest and Defense Commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 以右驍衞將軍常樂郭知運爲副使，與太僕少卿王晙帥兵擊之。

translations.literal: Right Brave Guard General Changyue Guo Ziyun was made vice commissioner, and together with Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Wang Jun they led troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Right Swift Guard General Guo Ziyun of Changyue was made vice commissioner; with Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Wang Jun he led troops against them.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，大募勇士，詣河、隴就訥教習。

translations.literal: Day xinsi, brave warriors were recruited on a large scale and sent to He and Long to receive training under Ne.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day brave men were recruited in large numbers and sent to He and Long to train under Ne.

sentences.zh: 初，鄯州都督楊矩以九曲之地與吐蕃，其地肥饒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Protector of Zheng Prefecture Yang Ju had ceded the Nine Bends territory to Tibet; the land was rich and fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zheng Prefecture Protector Yang Ju had ceded the Nine Bends to Tibet—land rich and fertile.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃就之畜牧，因以入寇，矩悔懼自殺。

translations.literal: Tibet came there to pasture livestock and thereby launched raids; Ju, filled with remorse and fear, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet pastured there and used the ground to raid; Yang Ju, stricken with remorse and fear, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，太子賓客薛謙光獻武後所制《豫州鼎銘》，其末云：「上玄降鑒，方建隆基。」

translations.literal: Day yiyou, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Xue Qianguang presented the "Inscription on the Yuzhou Cauldron" composed by Empress Wu, its closing words reading: "The Supreme Deity sends down insight—founding Longji is now at hand."
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day, Heir Apparent Mentor Xue Qianguang presented Empress Wu's "Inscription on the Yuzhou Cauldron," whose closing line reads: "Heaven sends down its sign—Longji shall be established."

sentences.zh: 以爲上受命之符。

translations.literal: This was taken as a token of the emperor's receipt of the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: This was taken as proof of the emperor's Mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 姚崇表賀，且請宣示史官，頒告中外。

translations.literal: Yao Chong submitted congratulations and also requested it be proclaimed to the historiographers and announced within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong offered congratulations and asked that it be proclaimed to the historiographers and announced throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：日食不驗，太史之過也；

translations.literal: Sima Guang remarks: When a solar eclipse failed to occur, that was the Grand Astrologer's error;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: When a predicted eclipse failed to occur, that was the court astronomer's fault;

sentences.zh: 而君臣相賀，是誣天也。

translations.literal: yet ruler and ministers congratulated one another—this was deceiving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: yet ruler and ministers congratulated one another—that was deceiving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 采偶然之文以爲符命，小臣之諂也；

translations.literal: Seizing upon accidental words as proof of mandate—this is a petty official's flattery;
translations.idiomatic: Seizing on chance words as proof of destiny is a petty official's flattery;

sentences.zh: 而宰相因而實之，是侮其君也。

translations.literal: yet the chief minister thereupon affirmed it—this is insulting one's lord.
translations.idiomatic: yet the chief minister affirmed it—that was insulting one's sovereign.

sentences.zh: 上誣於天，下侮其君，以明皇之明，姚崇之賢，猶不免於是，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: Above they deceived Heaven; below they insulted their lord—yet with Emperor Ming's brilliance and Yao Chong's worth, they still could not avoid this. Is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Deceiving Heaven above and insulting the sovereign below—and with Emperor Ming's brilliance and Yao Chong's virtue they still fell to this. How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 九月，戊申，上幸驪山溫湯。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day wushen, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the wushen day, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 敕以歲稔傷農，令諸州修常平倉法；

translations.literal: An edict, because abundant harvests harmed the farmers, ordered all prefectures to restore the ever-normal granary regulations;
translations.idiomatic: An edict, noting that bumper harvests hurt farmers, ordered all prefectures to restore the ever-normal granary system;

sentences.zh: 江、嶺、淮、浙、劍南地下濕，不堪貯積，不在此例。

translations.literal: the Jiang, Ling, Huai, Zhe, and Jiannan regions have damp ground unsuitable for storage and were not included in this rule.
translations.idiomatic: the Jiang, Ling, Huai, Zhe, and Jiannan regions, whose damp soil could not sustain storage, were exempt.

sentences.zh: 突厥可汗默啜衰老，昏虐愈甚；

translations.literal: The Türk qaghan Mojilian had grown old and feeble, and his dim tyranny grew ever worse;
translations.idiomatic: The Türk qaghan Mojilian had grown old and feeble, and his tyranny ever more benighted;

sentences.zh: 壬子，葛邏祿等部落詣涼州降。

translations.literal: Day renzi, the Karluk and other tribes came to Liangzhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day the Karluk and other tribes came to Liangzhou to surrender.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，吐蕃復寇渭源。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Tibet again raided Wei River source.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Tibet again raided Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，上下詔欲親征，發兵十餘萬人，馬四萬匹。

translations.literal: Day bingchen, the emperor issued an edict declaring his wish to campaign in person, mobilizing more than one hundred thousand troops and forty thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day the emperor issued an edict declaring his intent to campaign in person, mobilizing over one hundred thousand troops and forty thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 戊午，上還宮。

translations.literal: Day wuwu, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 甲子，薛訥與吐蕃戰於武街，大破之。

translations.literal: Day jiazi, Xue Ne fought Tibet at Wujie and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day Xue Ne fought Tibet at Wujie and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 時太僕少卿隴右群牧使王晙帥所部二千人與訥會擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and Longyou pasturage commissioner Wang Jun led two thousand men of his command to join Ne in striking Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and Longyou Pasturage Commissioner Wang Jun led two thousand of his men to join Ne against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 坌達延將吐蕃十萬屯大來谷，選勇士七百，衣胡服，夜襲之，多置鼓角於其後五里，前軍遇敵大呼，後人鳴鼓角以應之。

translations.literal: Bendayan commanded one hundred thousand Tibetans encamped at Dalai Valley; he selected seven hundred brave warriors, clad them in barbarian dress, and at night launched a raid—many drums and horns were placed five li to their rear; when the vanguard met the enemy they shouted loudly, and those behind sounded drums and horns in response.
translations.idiomatic: Bendayan held one hundred thousand Tibetans at Dalai Valley; Wang Jun chose seven hundred brave men, dressed them in foreign garb, and struck by night—drums and horns were posted five li to the rear; the vanguard shouted on contact, and men behind answered with drums and horns.

sentences.zh: 虜以爲大軍至，驚懼，自相殺傷，死者萬計。

translations.literal: The barbarians thought a great army had arrived; in panic and fear they killed and wounded one another, dead numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy thought a great army had arrived; in panic they turned on one another, and tens of thousands died.

sentences.zh: 訥時在武街，去大來谷二十里，虜軍塞其中間；

translations.literal: Ne was then at Wujie, twenty li from Dalai Valley, with the barbarian army blocking the space between;
translations.idiomatic: Ne was at Wujie, twenty li from Dalai Valley, with the enemy force blocking the gap between them;

sentences.zh: 晙復夜出兵襲之，虜大潰，始得與訥軍合。

translations.literal: Jun again went out by night to attack; the barbarians broke and fled in complete rout, and only then could he unite with Ne's army.
translations.idiomatic: Jun struck again by night; the enemy broke completely, and only then could he join Ne's force.

sentences.zh: 同追奔至洮水，復戰於長城堡，又敗之，前後殺獲數萬人。

translations.literal: Together they pursued the fleeing enemy to the Tao River, fought again at Changcheng Fort, defeated them once more—in all, tens of thousands were killed and captured before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Together they pursued the fugitives to the Tao River, fought again at Changcheng Fort and routed them once more—in all, tens of thousands were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 豐安軍使王海賓戰死。

translations.literal: Feng'an Army commissioner Wang Haibin died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Feng'an Army Commissioner Wang Haibin fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，敕罷親征。

translations.literal: Day yichou, an edict canceled the planned personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day an edict canceled the planned personal campaign.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，姚崇、盧懷慎等奏：「頃者吐蕃以河爲境，神龍中尚公主，遂逾河築城，置獨山、九曲兩軍，去積石三百里，又於河上造橋。

translations.literal: Day wuchen, Yao Chong, Lu Huaiqian, and others memorialized: "Recently Tibet took the river as its border; in the Shenlong era a princess was married to them, and they crossed the river to build fortifications, establishing the two garrisons of Dushan and Nine Bends three hundred li from Jishi, and also built a bridge on the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day Yao Chong, Lu Huaiqian, and others memorialized: "Recently Tibet has taken the river as its border; in the Shenlong era a princess was married to them, and they crossed the river to build forts, establishing the Dushan and Nine Bends garrisons three hundred li from Jishi, and also built a bridge across the river.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃既叛，宜毀橋拔城。」

translations.literal: Now that Tibet has rebelled, the bridge should be destroyed and the fortifications dismantled."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Tibet has rebelled, the bridge should be destroyed and the forts abandoned."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 以王海賓之子忠嗣爲朝散大夫、尚輦奉御，養之宮中。

translations.literal: Wang Haibin's son Zhongsi was made Grand Master of Palace Leisure and Palace Equipage Attendant and reared within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Haibin's son Zhongsi was made Grand Master of Palace Leisure and Palace Equipage Attendant and raised in the palace.

sentences.zh: 己巳，突厥可汗默啜又遣使求昏，上許以來歲迎公主。

translations.literal: Day jisi, the Türk qaghan Mojilian again sent envoys requesting marriage; the emperor agreed to welcome a princess in the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day the Türk qaghan Mojilian again sent envoys seeking a marriage alliance; the emperor agreed to welcome a princess the following year.

sentences.zh: 突厥十姓胡祿屋等諸部詣北庭請降，命都護郭虔瓘撫存之。

translations.literal: The various tribes of the Ten Surnames of the Türks, Hulüwu and others, came to Beiting to request surrender; Protector Guo Qianzhen was ordered to comfort and keep them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Surname Türk tribes led by Hulüwu came to Beiting to surrender; Protector Guo Qianzhen was ordered to receive and settle them.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，命左驍衞郎將尉遲瑰使於吐蕃，宣慰金城公主。

translations.literal: Day yiyou, Left Swift Cavalry Guard Commandant Yuchi Gui was dispatched as envoy to Tibet to console Princess Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day Left Swift Guard Commandant Yuchi Gui was sent as envoy to Tibet to console Princess Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣其大臣宗俄因矛至洮水請和，用敵國禮；

translations.literal: Tibet sent its minister Zong'eyinmao to the Tao River to request peace, using the etiquette due an equal state;
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent its minister Zong'eyinmao to the Tao River to sue for peace, using the protocol reserved for equal states;

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 自是連歲犯邊。

translations.literal: From this they violated the borders year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they raided the frontier year after year.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛卯，葬殤皇帝。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day xinmao, the prematurely deceased emperor was buried.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the xinmao day, Emperor Shang was buried.

sentences.zh: 丙申，遣左散騎常侍解琬詣北庭宣慰突厥降者，隨便宜區處。

translations.literal: Day bingchen, Left Gentleman Attendant at Leisure Xie Wan was dispatched to Beiting to console the surrendering Türks and dispose matters as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Wan was sent to Beiting to console the surrendering Türks and handle matters as local conditions required.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬戌，沙陀金山入朝。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day renxu, Shatuo Jinshan came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the renxu day, Shatuo Jinshan came to court.

sentences.zh: 甲子，置隴右節度大使，領鄯、奉、河、渭、蘭、臨、武、洮、岷、郭、疊、宕十二州，以隴右防禦副使郭知運爲之。

translations.literal: Day jiazi, the Longyou circuit grand commissioner was established, governing the twelve prefectures of Shan, Feng, He, Wei, Lan, Lin, Wu, Tao, Min, Guo, Die, and Dang; Longyou defense vice commissioner Guo Zhiyun was appointed to the post.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day a Longyou circuit grand commissioner was created, with jurisdiction over twelve prefectures—Shan, Feng, He, Wei, Lan, Lin, Wu, Tao, Min, Guo, Die, and Dang—and Longyou Defense Vice Commissioner Guo Zhiyun was named to the office.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，立皇子嗣真爲鄫王，嗣初爲鄂王，嗣玄爲鄄王。

translations.literal: Day yichou, the emperor's sons Sizhen, Sichu, and Sixuan were invested as Prince of Zeng, Prince of E, and Prince of Juancheng respectively.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day the emperor invested his sons Sizhen as Prince of Zeng, Sichu as Prince of E, and Sixuan as Prince of Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，立郢王嗣謙爲皇太子。

translations.literal: Day xinsi, Prince of Ying Siqian was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day Prince of Ying Siqian was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 嗣真，上之長子，母曰劉華妃。

translations.literal: Sizhen was the emperor's eldest son; his mother was Consort Liu Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen was the emperor's eldest son, born to Consort Liu Hua.

sentences.zh: 嗣謙，次子也，母曰趙麗妃；

translations.literal: Siqian was the second son; his mother was Consort Zhao Li;
translations.idiomatic: Siqian was the second son, born to Consort Zhao Li;

sentences.zh: 麗妃以倡進，有寵於上，故立之。

translations.literal: Consort Li had entered the palace as a singing-girl performer and enjoyed the emperor's favor; therefore he was established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li had been brought into the palace from the ranks of performers and held the emperor's favor, which was why her son was made heir.

sentences.zh: 是歲，置幽州節度、經略、鎭守大使，領幽、易、平、檀、媯、燕六州。

translations.literal: That year the Youzhou circuit, frontier strategy, and garrison grand commissioner was established, governing the six prefectures of You, Yi, Ping, Tan, Gui, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: That year a Youzhou circuit commissioner with authority over frontier strategy and garrison defense was created, with jurisdiction over You, Yi, Ping, Tan, Gui, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 突騎施可汗守忠之弟遮弩恨所分部落少於其兄，遂叛入突厥，請爲鄕導，以伐守忠。

translations.literal: Zhenu, younger brother of Turgish qaghan Shouzhong, resented receiving fewer tribes than his elder brother; he therefore rebelled and fled to the Türks, requesting to serve as guide in an attack on Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenu, younger brother of the Turgish qaghan Shouzhong, resented the smaller share of tribes allotted to him and defected to the Türks, offering to guide them against his brother.

sentences.zh: 默啜遣兵二萬擊守忠，虜之而還。

translations.literal: Mojilian dispatched twenty thousand troops to strike Shouzhong, captured him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mojilian sent twenty thousand men against Shouzhong, took him captive, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 謂遮弩曰：「汝叛其兄，何有於我！」

translations.literal: He said to Zhenu: "You betrayed your elder brother—what loyalty can you show me!"
translations.idiomatic: He said to Zhenu, "You betrayed your own brother—why should I trust you!

sentences.zh: 遂並殺之。

translations.literal: and thereupon had them both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he had them both put to death.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯，以盧懷慎檢校吏部尚書兼黃門監。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day guimao, Lu Huaiqian was made acting Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Supervisor of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's guimao day, Lu Huaiqian was appointed acting Minister of Personnel and concurrently Supervisor of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 懷慎清謹儉素，不營資產，雖貴爲卿相，所得俸賜，隨散親舊。

translations.literal: Huaiqian was pure, cautious, frugal, and plain; he did not accumulate property. Though elevated to minister and chief minister, whatever salary and gifts he received he distributed at once among kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiqian was upright, cautious, and austere, never building up private wealth. Even after rising to the highest offices, he gave away his salary and gifts as soon as they arrived, sharing them with relatives and old acquaintances.

sentences.zh: 妻子不免饑寒，所居不蔽風雨。

translations.literal: His wife and children could not escape hunger and cold; the dwelling where he lived could not keep out wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children still knew hunger and cold, and his house could barely keep out wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 姚崇嘗有子喪，謁告十餘日，政事委積。

translations.literal: Yao Chong once had a son die; he requested leave for more than ten days, and official business piled up unattended.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong once took more than ten days' leave to mourn a son, government business piled up unhandled.

sentences.zh: 懷慎不能決，惶恐入謝於上。

translations.literal: Huaiqian could not decide the matters and, in fear and trepidation, entered to apologize to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiqian could not resolve the backlog and, deeply troubled, went before the emperor to apologize.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕以天下事委姚崇，以卿坐鎭雅俗耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have entrusted the affairs of the empire to Yao Chong; as for you, you are merely to sit and keep refined and popular custom in order."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have entrusted the affairs of the realm to Yao Chong; your role is simply to preside over court decorum and public manners."

sentences.zh: 崇既出，須臾，裁決俱盡，頗有得色，顧謂紫微舍人齊澣曰：「余爲相，可比何人？」

translations.literal: After Chong came out, in a short while he had decided them all and wore a rather satisfied look; turning, he said to Palace Secretariat drafter Qi Huan: "As chief minister, whom may I be compared to?"
translations.idiomatic: When Chong returned, he cleared the entire backlog within moments, looking quite pleased with himself. He turned to Palace Secretariat drafter Qi Huan and asked, "As chief minister, whom would you compare me to?"

sentences.zh: 澣未對，崇曰：「何如管、晏？」

translations.literal: Huan had not yet answered when Chong said: "How about Guan Zhong and Yan Ying?"
translations.idiomatic: Before Huan could answer, Chong said, "How do I compare with Guan Zhong and Yan Ying?"

sentences.zh: 澣曰：「管、晏之法雖不能施於後，猶能沒身。

translations.literal: Huan said: "Although the methods of Guan and Yan could not be applied after their deaths, they could still endure through the end of their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Huan replied, "Guan and Yan's policies, though they could not outlast them, at least held steady through their lifetimes.

sentences.zh: 公所爲法，隨復更之，似不及也。」

translations.literal: The laws you enact are changed again as soon as they are made—it seems you do not reach that level."
translations.idiomatic: Your policies are revised almost as soon as you enact them—you fall somewhat short of them, I think."

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「然則竟如何？」

translations.literal: Chong said: "Then in the end, how am I?"
translations.idiomatic: Chong asked, "Then how would you rank me?"

sentences.zh: 澣曰：「公可謂救時之相耳。」

translations.literal: Huan said: "You may be called a chief minister who saves the age."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "You might be called a chief minister who rescues his own times."

sentences.zh: 崇喜，投筆曰：「救時之相，豈易得乎！」

translations.literal: Chong was pleased, tossed down his brush, and said: "A chief minister who saves the age—is that not hard to come by!"
translations.idiomatic: Chong was delighted. He tossed down his brush and exclaimed, "A chief minister who rescues his times—is that so easily found!"

sentences.zh: 懷慎與崇同爲相，自以才不及崇，每事推之，時人謂之「伴食宰相。」

translations.literal: Huaiqian served as chief minister together with Chong; believing his own talent fell short of Chong's, he deferred to him in every matter, and people of the time called him "the dinner-table chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiqian served alongside Chong as chief minister. Judging himself less capable, he deferred to Chong on every matter, and contemporaries dubbed him "the dinner-table chief minister."

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：昔鮑叔之於管仲，子皮之於子產，皆位居其上，能知其賢而下之，授以國政；

translations.literal: Sima Guang remarks: In antiquity Bao Shuya toward Guan Zhong, and Zipi toward Zichan—both stood above them in rank, yet recognized their worth and stepped below them, entrusting them with state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: Long ago Bao Shuya with Guan Zhong, and Zipi with Zichan—though each stood above the other in rank, recognized his worth, yielded place to him, and entrusted him with the government;

sentences.zh: 孔子美之。

translations.literal: Confucius praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius praised such men.

sentences.zh: 曹參自謂不及蕭何，一遵其法，無所變更；

translations.literal: Cao Shen declared himself inferior to Xiao He, followed his laws entirely, and changed nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shen held himself inferior to Xiao He, adhered wholly to his policies, and changed nothing;

sentences.zh: 漢業以成。

translations.literal: and the Han enterprise was thereby accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: and the Han dynasty prospered as a result.

sentences.zh: 夫不肖用事，爲其僚者，愛身保祿而從之，不顧國家之安危，是誠罪人也。

translations.literal: When an unworthy man holds power, colleagues who cherish their persons, preserve their stipends, and follow him without regard for the state's safety or peril are indeed criminals.
translations.idiomatic: When an unworthy man holds power, colleagues who cling to office and salary, follow him blindly, and ignore the nation's welfare are truly guilty men.

sentences.zh: 賢智用事，爲其僚者，愚惑以亂其治，專固以分其權，媢嫉以毀其功，愎戾以竊其名，是亦罪人也。

translations.literal: When a wise and able man holds power, colleagues who confuse and disorder his governance through folly, stubbornly divide his authority, envy and destroy his achievements, and perversely seize his reputation are also criminals.
translations.idiomatic: When a worthy man holds power, colleagues who muddle his governance with foolish interference, carve up his authority, envy and undermine his achievements, or arrogantly steal his credit are criminals as well.

sentences.zh: 崇，唐之賢相，懷慎與之同心戮力，以濟明皇太平之政，夫何罪哉！

translations.literal: Chong was a worthy chief minister of Tang; Huaiqian joined him in one heart and shared effort to complete Emperor Ming's era of great peace—what crime was there in that!
translations.idiomatic: Chong was a worthy chief minister of Tang, and Huaiqian worked with him wholeheartedly to bring about Emperor Ming's age of peace—where was the fault in that!

sentences.zh: 《秦誓》曰：「如有一介臣，斷斷猗，無它技；

translations.literal: The "Oath of Qin" says: "If there is one loyal minister, steadfast and upright, with no other skill;
translations.idiomatic: The "Oath of Qin" says, "If there is one loyal minister, steadfast and upright, possessing no other talent;

sentences.zh: 其心休休焉，其如有容；

translations.literal: his heart is generous and broad, as if he has capacity to spare;
translations.idiomatic: his heart is generous and broad, as though he has room to spare;

sentences.zh: 人之有技，若己有之，人之彥聖，其心好之，不啻如自其口出，是能容之，以保我子孫黎民，亦職有利哉。」

translations.literal: when others have skill he treats it as his own; when others are wise and sage his heart delights in them, not less than if the words came from his own mouth—such a one can be tolerant, and thereby preserve our descendants and the common people: this too is a profitable duty."
translations.idiomatic: when others possess skill he rejoices as if it were his own; when others are wise and good his heart delights in them as though he himself had spoken the praise—such a man can be tolerant, and by tolerance preserve our descendants and the people: this too is a worthy calling."

sentences.zh: 懷慎之謂矣。

translations.literal: This describes Huaiqian.
translations.idiomatic: That describes Huaiqian.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫宋璟坐監朝堂杖人杖輕，貶睦州刺史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Song Jing was demoted to prefect of Mu Prefecture on the charge that, while supervising beatings in the court hall, the strokes he ordered were too light.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Song Jing was demoted to prefect of Mu Prefecture for supervising court floggings with strokes deemed too light.

sentences.zh: 突厥十勝降者前後萬餘帳。

translations.literal: Surrendered Türks of the Ten Surnames numbered more than ten thousand households before and after.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Türk households of the Ten Surnames surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 高麗莫離支文簡，十姓之婿也，二月，與□夾跌都督思泰等亦自突厥帥眾來降；

translations.literal: Goguryeo molichie Wenjian, son-in-law of the Ten Surnames, in the second month together with Adie tribal commissioner Sitai and others also led their followers from the Türks to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Wenjian, a Goguryeo molichie and son-in-law of the Ten Surnames, came in the second month with Adie Tribal Commissioner Sitai and others, leading their followers from the Türks to surrender;

sentences.zh: 制皆以河南地處之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all be settled on lands south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that all be settled south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 三月，胡祿屋酋長支匐忌等入朝。

translations.literal: Third month, Hulüwu tribal chieftain Zhipuji and others came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Hulüwu chieftain Zhipuji and others came to court.

sentences.zh: 上以十姓降者浸多，夏，四月，庚申，以右羽林大將軍薛訥爲涼州鎭大總管，赤水等軍並受節度，居涼州；

translations.literal: Because surrendered members of the Ten Surnames were gradually increasing, in summer, fourth month, day gengshen, Right Forest of Feathers Guard General Xue Ne was made grand general of Liang Prefecture garrison; the Chishui and other armies all came under his command, and he was stationed at Liangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: As surrenders from the Ten Surnames mounted, in summer, on the fourth month's gengshen day, Right Forest Guard General Xue Ne was made grand commander of the Liangzhou garrison, with the Chishui and other armies under his command, stationed at Liangzhou;

sentences.zh: 左衞大將軍郭虔瓘爲朔州鎭大總管，和戎等軍並受節度，居并州，勒兵以備默啜。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Guo Qianzhen was made grand general of Shuozhou garrison; the Herong and other armies all came under his command, and he was stationed at Bingzhou, mustering troops to guard against Mojilian.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Guo Qianzhen was made grand commander of the Shuozhou garrison, with the Herong and other armies under his command, stationed at Bingzhou to muster forces against Mojilian.

sentences.zh: 默啜發兵擊葛邏祿、胡祿屋、鼠尼施等，屢破之；

translations.literal: Mojilian dispatched troops to strike the Qarluk, Hulüwu, Shunishi, and others, repeatedly defeating them;
