translations.idiomatic: Mojilian sent troops against the Qarluk, Hulüwu, Shunishi, and others, defeating them repeatedly;

sentences.zh: 敕北庭都護湯嘉惠、左散騎常侍解琬等發兵救之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Beiting Protector Tang Jiahui, Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Wan, and others to dispatch troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Beiting Protector Tang Jiahui, Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Xie Wan, and others to send relief forces.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬辰，敕嘉惠等與葛邏祿、胡祿屋、鼠尼施及定邊道十總管阿史那獻互相應援。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day renchen, an edict ordered Jiahui and the others to give one another mutual support with the Qarluk, Hulüwu, Shunishi, and Dingbian Circuit grand general Ashina Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the renchen day, an edict directed Jiahui and the others to coordinate with the Qarluk, Hulüwu, Shunishi, and Dingbian Circuit Grand General Ashina Xian in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 山東大蝗，民或於田旁焚香膜拜設祭而不敢殺，姚崇奏遣御史督州縣捕而瘞之。

translations.literal: Great locust swarms struck east of the mountains; common people sometimes burned incense, bowed in worship, and set out offerings beside the fields but dared not kill them. Yao Chong memorialized dispatching censors to supervise prefectures and counties in capturing and burying them.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravaged the eastern provinces; peasants sometimes burned incense, bowed, and made offerings beside the fields but dared not kill the insects. Yao Chong memorialized sending censors to supervise local officials in capturing and burying the swarms.

sentences.zh: 議者以爲蝗眾多，除不可盡；

translations.literal: Critics held that the locusts were too numerous and could not all be exterminated;
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that the locusts were too numerous to exterminate entirely;

sentences.zh: 上亦疑之。

translations.literal: the emperor also had doubts.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor himself was skeptical.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「今蝗滿山東，河南、北之人，流亡殆盡，豈可坐視食苗，曾不救乎！

translations.literal: Chong said: "Now locusts fill the east of the mountains; the people of Henan and north of the Yellow River have nearly all become refugees—how can we sit and watch them devour the seedlings and not rescue them!
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "Locusts now cover the eastern provinces; the people of Henan and the lands north of the river have fled until almost none remain—how can we sit idle while they devour the crops!

sentences.zh: 借使除之不盡，猶勝養以成災。」

translations.literal: Even if we cannot exterminate them all, that is still better than nurturing them until disaster is complete."
translations.idiomatic: Even if we cannot destroy them all, that is still better than letting them breed a full catastrophe."

sentences.zh: 以乃從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon agreed.

sentences.zh: 盧懷慎以爲殺蝗太多，恐傷和氣。

translations.literal: Lu Huaiqian held that killing too many locusts might harm the harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huaiqian feared that killing so many locusts might disturb cosmic harmony.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「昔楚莊吞蛭而愈疾，孫叔殺蛇而致福，奈何不忍於蝗，而忍人之饑死乎？

translations.literal: Chong said: "In antiquity King Zhuang of Chu swallowed a leech and was cured of illness; Sunshu Ao killed a snake and thereby brought blessing—how can you be unwilling to harm locusts yet willing to let people starve to death?
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, "King Zhuang of Chu once swallowed a leech and was cured; Sunshu Ao killed a snake and brought blessing—how can we shrink from killing locusts yet accept human starvation?

sentences.zh: 若使殺蝗有禍，崇請當之！」

translations.literal: If killing locusts brings calamity, Chong requests to bear it himself!"
translations.idiomatic: If killing locusts brings retribution, let the blame fall on me!"

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day gengchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰相曰：「朕每讀書有所疑滯，無從質問；

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chief ministers: "Whenever I read books and encounter doubts I cannot resolve, I have no one from whom to seek clarification;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers, "When I read and encounter passages I cannot resolve, I have no one to question;

sentences.zh: 可選儒學之士，日使入內侍讀。」

translations.literal: select scholars of Confucian learning and have them enter daily to attend and read with me."
translations.idiomatic: select learned Confucian scholars and have them attend me daily for reading and discussion."

sentences.zh: 盧懷慎薦太常卿馬懷素。

translations.literal: Lu Huaiqian recommended Court of Imperial Sacrifices Minister Ma Huaisu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huaiqian recommended Court of Imperial Sacrifices Minister Ma Huaisu.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊寅，以懷素爲左散騎常侍，使與右散騎常侍褚無量更日侍讀。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day wuyin, Huaisu was made Left Attendant-in-Ordinary and ordered to attend the emperor in reading on alternate days with Right Attendant-in-Ordinary Chu Wuliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the wuyin day, Huaisu was appointed Left Attendant-in-Ordinary and assigned to attend the emperor on alternate days with Right Attendant-in-Ordinary Chu Wuliang.

sentences.zh: 每至閣門，令乘肩輿以進；

translations.literal: Whenever they reached the Gate of the Inner Court, they were ordered to enter by sedan chair;
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the inner gate they were carried in by sedan chair;

sentences.zh: 或在別館道遠，聽於宮中乘馬。

translations.literal: if they were at a distant lodge and the way was long, they were permitted to ride horses within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: if lodged far away they were even permitted to ride horses within the palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 親送迎之，待以師傅之禮。

translations.literal: The emperor personally saw them off and received them, treating them with the etiquette due a tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally escorted them in and out, treating them with the respect owed a tutor.

sentences.zh: 以無量羸老，特爲之造腰輿，在內殿令內侍舁之。

translations.literal: Because Wuliang was frail and aged, a special waist-borne sedan was made for him; within the inner hall palace attendants were ordered to carry him in it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wuliang was frail with age, a special carrying-chair was built for him, and inside the inner hall palace attendants were assigned to bear him in it.

sentences.zh: 九姓思結都督磨散等來降；

translations.literal: Nine-Surname Sijie tribal commissioner Mosan and others came to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Nine-Surname Sijie Tribal Commissioner Mosan and others surrendered;

sentences.zh: 己未，悉除官遣還。

translations.literal: Day jiwei, all were granted offices and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day all were given offices and sent home.

sentences.zh: 西南蠻寇邊，遣右驍衞將軍李玄道發戎、瀘、夔、巴、梁、鳳等州兵三萬人並舊屯兵討之。

translations.literal: Southwestern barbarians raided the frontier; Right Swift Guard General Li Xuandao was dispatched to mobilize thirty thousand troops from the prefectures of Rong, Lu, Kui, Ba, Liang, and Feng together with existing garrison forces to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern tribes raided the frontier; Right Swift Guard General Li Xuandao was sent to raise thirty thousand men from Rong, Lu, Kui, Ba, Liang, and Feng, together with existing garrison troops, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以涼州大總管薛訥爲朔方道行軍大總管，太僕卿呂延祚、靈州刺史杜賓客副之，以討突厥。

translations.literal: Day renxu, Liangzhou grand general Xue Ne was made campaign grand general of the Shuofang Circuit; Minister of the Imperial Stud Lü Yanzuo and Ling Prefecture prefect Du Binkè were made his deputies to attack the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day Liangzhou Grand Commander Xue Ne was made campaign commander of the Shuofang Circuit, with Minister of the Imperial Stud Lü Yanzuo and Ling Prefecture Prefect Du Binkè as his deputies, to campaign against the Türks.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上幸鳳泉湯；

translations.literal: Day jiazi, the emperor visited the Fengquan Hot Springs;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day the emperor visited the Fengquan Hot Springs;

sentences.zh: 十一月，己卯，還京師。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day jimao, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the jimao day, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 劉幽求自杭州剌史徙郴州剌史，憤恚，甲申，卒於道。

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu was transferred from prefect of Hang Prefecture to prefect of Chen Prefecture; indignant and resentful, on day jiashen he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu was transferred from Hang Prefecture to Chen Prefecture; consumed by anger and resentment, he died on the road on the jiashen day.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以左羽林大將軍郭虔瓘兼安西大都護、四鎭經略大使。

translations.literal: Day dingyou, Left Forest of Feathers Guard General Guo Qianzhen was made concurrently Protector-General of Anxi and frontier strategy commissioner of the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day Left Forest Guard General Guo Qianzhen was appointed concurrently Protector-General of Anxi and frontier strategy commissioner over the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 虔瓘請募關中兵萬人詣安西討擊，皆給遞馱及熟食；

translations.literal: Qianzhen requested recruiting ten thousand Guanzhong troops to proceed to Anxi for punitive strikes, all to be supplied with relay mounts and prepared rations;
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhen requested recruiting ten thousand Guanzhong troops for a punitive expedition to Anxi, with relay mounts and prepared rations supplied to all;

sentences.zh: 敕許之。

translations.literal: an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: an edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠韋湊上疏，以爲：「今西域服從，雖或時有小盜竊，舊鎭兵足以制之。

translations.literal: Master of Works Wei Cou submitted a memorial, stating: "The Western Regions now submit; though there may occasionally be small thefts and raids, the old garrison troops are sufficient to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Works Wei Cou submitted a memorial arguing, "The Western Regions now submit to us; occasional petty raids can be handled by the existing garrison forces.

sentences.zh: 關中常宜充實，以強幹弱枝。

translations.literal: Guanzhong ought always to be kept full and strong, strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong should always be kept strong—the trunk fortified, the branches kept lean.

sentences.zh: 自頃西北二虜寇邊，凡在丁壯，征行略盡，豈宜更募驍勇，遠資荒服！

translations.literal: Recently the two barbarians of the northwest have raided the frontier; among all able-bodied men, those called to campaign have nearly all been exhausted—how can we further recruit fierce warriors to supply distant wilderness domains!
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern raids have already drained the region of able-bodied men—why recruit more warriors to feed distant frontier outposts!

sentences.zh: 又，一萬徵人行六千餘里，鹹給遞馱熟食，道次州縣，將何以供！

translations.literal: Moreover, ten thousand men on campaign traveling more than six thousand li, all supplied with relay mounts and prepared rations—what will the prefectures and counties along the route have to provide!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, ten thousand men marching more than six thousand li, each supplied with relay mounts and rations—what will the counties along the route have left to give!

sentences.zh: 秦、隴之西，戸口漸少，涼州已往，沙磧悠然，遣彼居人，如何取濟？

translations.literal: West of Qin and Long the population is gradually shrinking; beyond Liangzhou lies endless desert sands—how are the people there to be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: West of Qin and Long the population is dwindling; beyond Liangzhou lies nothing but desert—how are the people there to sustain such a host?

sentences.zh: 縱令必克，其獲幾何？

translations.literal: Even if victory were certain, how much would be gained?
translations.idiomatic: Even assuming certain victory, what would we gain?

sentences.zh: 儻稽天誅，無乃甚損！

translations.literal: If Heaven's punishment were delayed, would not the loss be very great!
translations.idiomatic: If the campaign failed, would not the damage be enormous!

sentences.zh: 請計所用、所得，校其多少，則知利害。

translations.literal: I request calculating what would be spent and what would be gained, comparing the two, and then the advantage or harm will be known.
translations.idiomatic: Calculate the cost against the gain, and the wisdom of the plan will be plain.

sentences.zh: 昔唐堯之代，兼愛夷、夏，中外乂安；

translations.literal: In the age of Tang Yao, he equally cherished barbarian and Chinese, and within and without were well governed and at peace;
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Emperor Yao, barbarian and Chinese alike were embraced, and the realm within and without was at peace;

sentences.zh: 漢武窮兵遠征，雖多克獲，而中國疲耗。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han exhausted the army in distant campaigns; though he conquered and captured much, the Central Kingdom was worn down and depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han exhausted the realm in distant campaigns; though he won many victories, the heartland was drained.

sentences.zh: 今論帝王之盛德者，皆歸唐堯，不歸漢武；

translations.literal: Today those who discuss the supreme virtue of emperors all ascribe it to Tang Yao, not to Emperor Wu of Han;
translations.idiomatic: Today when men praise imperial greatness they honor Emperor Yao, not Emperor Wu;

sentences.zh: 況邀功不成者，復何足比議乎！」

translations.literal: how much less is a man who seeks merit yet achieves nothing worth bringing into the comparison!"
translations.idiomatic: how much less should we compare a campaign that seeks glory yet achieves nothing!"

sentences.zh: 時姚崇亦以虔瓘之策爲不然。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Chong also held Qianzhen's plan to be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong likewise opposed Qianzhen's plan.

sentences.zh: 既而虔瓘卒無功。

translations.literal: Before long Qianzhen in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Qianzhen's expedition came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 初，監察御史張孝嵩奉使廓州還，陳磧西利害，請往察其形勢；

translations.literal: Earlier, Supervising Censor Zhang Xiaosong, returning from a mission to Kuo Prefecture, set forth the advantages and harms of the region west of the desert and requested to go inspect its strategic situation;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Supervising Censor Zhang Xiaosong, returning from a mission to Kuo Prefecture, outlined the strategic situation west of the desert and asked to reconnoiter the region;

sentences.zh: 上許之，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: the emperor approved this and permitted him to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed and authorized him to act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 枝汗那者，古烏孫也，內附歲久。

translations.literal: Warishana was ancient Wusun; it had submitted inward and been attached for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Warishana was the ancient Wusun kingdom, long a Tang dependency.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃與大食共立阿了達爲王，發兵攻之，枝汗那王兵敗，奔安西求救。

translations.literal: Tibet and the Arabs jointly installed Alida as king and dispatched troops to attack it; the king of Warishana was defeated in battle and fled to Anxi to request rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet and the Arabs jointly installed Alida as king and attacked Warishana; its king was defeated and fled to Anxi for help.

sentences.zh: 孝嵩謂都護呂休璟曰：「不救則無以號令西域。」

translations.literal: Xiaosong said to Protector Lü Xiujing: "If we do not rescue them, we will have no means to command the Western Regions."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosong told Protector Lü Xiujing, "If we fail to rescue them, we cannot command the Western Regions."

sentences.zh: 遂帥旁側戎落兵萬餘人，出龜茲西數千里，下數百城，長驅而進。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led more than ten thousand troops of neighboring barbarian settlements, went out several thousand li west of Kucha, reduced several hundred cities, and advanced at full drive.
translations.idiomatic: He then led more than ten thousand allied tribal troops west of Kucha for several thousand li, reducing hundreds of towns as he drove forward.

sentences.zh: 是月，攻阿了達於連城。

translations.literal: That month he attacked Alida at Liancheng.
translations.idiomatic: That month he attacked Alida at Liancheng.

sentences.zh: 孝嵩自擐甲督士卒急攻，自巳至酉，屠其三城，俘斬千餘級，阿了達與數騎逃入山谷。

translations.literal: Xiaosong himself donned armor and directed the troops in pressing the attack; from the si hour to the you hour he slaughtered three cities, capturing and beheading more than a thousand; Alida fled into the mountains with a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosong donned armor and personally directed a furious assault; from mid-morning to evening he stormed three cities, killing or capturing more than a thousand; Alida escaped into the hills with a handful of riders.

sentences.zh: 孝嵩傳檄諸國，威振西域，大食、康居、大宛、罽賓等八國皆遣使請降。

translations.literal: Xiaosong sent proclamations to the various states; his authority shook the Western Regions, and eight states including the Arabs, Kangju, Dayuan, and Jibin all dispatched envoys requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosong issued proclamations to the region; his prestige shook the Western Regions, and eight states—including the Arabs, Kangju, Dayuan, and Jibin—all sent envoys offering submission.

sentences.zh: 勒石紀功而還。

translations.literal: He carved stone to record his achievements and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He erected a stone monument to record his achievements and returned.

sentences.zh: 會有言其贓污者，坐系涼州獄，貶靈州兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: It happened that someone reported his corruption; for this he was imprisoned in Liangzhou and demoted to Military Staff Officer at Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward someone accused him of corruption; he was imprisoned in Liangzhou and demoted to military staff officer at Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹崔日知貪暴不法，御史大夫李傑將糾之，日知反構傑罪。

translations.literal: Cui Rizhi, Governor of Jingzhao, was greedy, violent, and lawless; Censor-in-Chief Li Jie was about to impeach him, but Rizhi in turn fabricated charges against Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rizhi, governor of Jingzhao, was greedy, violent, and lawless. When Censor-in-Chief Li Jie moved to impeach him, Rizhi turned the tables and fabricated charges against Jie.

sentences.zh: 十二月，侍御史楊瑒廷奏曰：「若糾彈之司，使奸人得而恐愒，則御史台可廢矣。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Attending Censor Yang Chang memorialized at court, saying: "If the offices charged with impeachment allow wicked men to intimidate them, then the Censorate might as well be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Attending Censor Yang Chang memorialized at court: "If the offices charged with impeachment can be intimidated by wicked men, the Censorate might as well be abolished."

sentences.zh: 上遽命傑視事如故，貶日知爲歙縣丞。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered Jie to resume his duties as before and demoted Rizhi to Assistant Magistrate of She County.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately restored Jie to his post and demoted Rizhi to assistant magistrate of She County.

sentences.zh: 或上言：「按察使徒煩擾公私，請精簡刺史、縣令，停按察使。」

translations.literal: Someone submitted to the emperor: "The surveillance commissioners only vex public and private interests without cause; please carefully select prefects and county magistrates and abolish the surveillance commissioners."
translations.idiomatic: Someone submitted to the emperor: "The surveillance commissioners only harass public and private interests to no purpose. Please carefully select prefects and county magistrates and abolish the surveillance commissioners."

sentences.zh: 上命召尚書省官議之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered officials of the Department of State Affairs summoned to deliberate on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered officials of the Department of State Affairs summoned to discuss the proposal.

sentences.zh: 姚崇以爲：「今止擇十使，猶患未盡得人，況天下三百餘州，縣多數倍，安得刺史、縣令皆稱其職乎！」

translations.literal: Yao Chong held: "Today, selecting only ten commissioners, we still worry we have not fully obtained fit men — how much more so when there are over three hundred prefectures under Heaven and counties are many times that number? How can every prefect and county magistrate perform his duties properly!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong argued: "Even when we choose only ten commissioners, we still fear we have not found enough capable men — and there are more than three hundred prefectures under Heaven, with counties many times that number. How can every prefect and county magistrate be equal to his office?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞韋玢奏：「郎官多不舉職，請沙汰，改授他官。」

translations.literal: Wei Bin, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, memorialized: "Many members of the department bureau neglect their duties; please cull them and reassign them to other offices."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bin, left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, memorialized: "Many department clerks neglect their duties. Please cull them and reassign them to other posts."

sentences.zh: 玢尋出爲刺史，宰相奏擬冀州，敕改小州。

translations.literal: Not long afterward Bin was sent out as a prefect; the chief ministers proposed appointing him to Jizhou, but an edict changed this to a smaller prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Bin was sent out as a prefect. The chief ministers proposed Jizhou, but an edict reassigned him to a smaller prefecture.

sentences.zh: 姚崇奏言：「台郎寬怠及不稱職，玢請沙汰，乃是奉公。

translations.literal: Yao Chong memorialized: "That the department clerks are lax and negligent and unfit for office, and that Bin requested a culling, was in fact discharging public duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong memorialized: "The department clerks are lax and unfit for office, and Bin's request to cull them was a matter of public duty.

sentences.zh: 台郎甫爾改官，玢即貶黜於外，議者皆謂郎官謗傷。

translations.literal: The department clerks had barely been reassigned when Bin was immediately demoted and sent out — commentators all said the clerks had slandered and injured him.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks had barely been reassigned when Bin was immediately demoted and sent out. Commentators all said the clerks had slandered him.

sentences.zh: 臣恐後來左右丞指以爲戒，則省事何從而舉矣！

translations.literal: Your subject fears that later Left and Right Vice Directors will point to this as a warning, and then how will the department dare to act!
translations.idiomatic: I fear that future left and right vice directors will take this as a warning, and then how will the department dare to act!

sentences.zh: 伏望聖慈祥察，使當官者無所疑懼。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will graciously examine this, so that those who hold office will have no doubts or fear."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will graciously consider this, so that officials in office will have no doubts or fear."

sentences.zh: 乃除冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was then appointed prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 突騎施守忠既死，默啜兵還，守忠部將蘇祿鳩集餘眾，爲之酋長。

translations.literal: After Shouzhong, khan of the Turgesh, had died and Mouyuchuo's troops returned, Shouzhong's lieutenant Suluo gathered the remaining force and made himself their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: After the Turgesh khan Shouzhong died and Mouyuchuo's army withdrew, Shouzhong's lieutenant Suluo gathered the survivors and made himself their chieftain.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿頗善綏撫，十姓部落稍稍歸之，有眾二十萬，遂據有西方，尋遣使入見。

translations.literal: Suluo was quite skilled at pacification; the tribes of the Ten Surnames gradually returned to him one by one. With a force of two hundred thousand he then held the western regions and soon sent envoys to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: Suluo proved adept at winning people over; the Ten Surnames tribes gradually returned to him until he commanded two hundred thousand men, held the western regions, and soon sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以蘇祿爲左羽林大將軍、金方道經略大使。

translations.literal: That year Suluo was appointed General of the Left Army of Brilliant Forest and Grand Commissioner for the Jinfang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That year Suluo was appointed general of the Left Army of Brilliant Forest and grand commissioner for the Jinfang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 皇后妹夫尚衣奉御長孫昕以細故與御史大夫李傑不協。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Xin, the Empress's brother-in-law and Director of Palace Attire, fell out with Censor-in-Chief Li Jie over a trifle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Xin, the empress's brother-in-law and director of palace attire, fell out with Censor-in-Chief Li Jie over a trifle.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，昕與其妹夫楊仙玉於里巷伺傑而毆之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Xin and his brother-in-law Yang Xianyu lay in wait for Jie in a back lane and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Xin and his brother-in-law Yang Xianyu lay in wait for Jie in a back lane and beat him.

sentences.zh: 傑上表自訴曰：「髮膚見毀，雖則育心，冠冕被陵，誠爲辱國。」

translations.literal: Jie submitted a memorial of self-accusation, saying: "Though injury to hair and skin may nourish the heart, violation of cap and regalia is truly a disgrace to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Jie submitted a memorial of protest: "Though injury to body and skin may be borne in private, an assault on cap and regalia is truly a disgrace to the state."

sentences.zh: 上大怒，命於朝堂杖殺，以謝百僚，仍以敕書慰傑曰：「昕等朕之密戚，不能訓導，使陵犯衣冠，雖置以極刑，未足謝罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered them beaten to death in the court hall as an apology to the officials; he also sent an edict comforting Jie, saying: "Xin and the others are my close kin; I failed to instruct and guide them, allowing them to violate the dignity of office — even imposing the utmost penalty is insufficient to atone for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered them beaten to death in the court hall as an apology to the officials. He also sent an edict comforting Jie: "Xin and the others are my close kin. I failed to instruct them, allowing them to violate the dignity of office — even the death penalty is insufficient to atone.

sentences.zh: 卿宜以剛腸疾惡，勿以凶人介意。」

translations.literal: You should keep a firm will and hate evil; do not take these wicked men to heart."
translations.idiomatic: Keep a firm will and hate evil; do not let these wicked men trouble you."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，宋王成器更名憲，申王成義更爲名摠。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Prince of Song Chengqì was given the new name Xian; Prince of Shen Chengyì was given the new name Zong.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Prince of Song Chengqì was renamed Xian, and Prince of Shen Chengyì was renamed Zong.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，隴右節度使郭虔瓘奏，奴石良才等八人皆有戰功，請除游擊將軍。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Guo Qianjin, Military Governor of Longyou, memorialized that eight men including the slave Shi Liangcai had all rendered military merit and requested they be appointed General of Guerrilla Warfare.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Guo Qianjin, military governor of Longyou, memorialized that eight men, including the slave Shi Liangcai, had all rendered military merit and requested they be appointed generals of guerrilla warfare.

sentences.zh: 敕下，盧懷慎等奏曰：「郭虔瓘恃其微效，輒侮彝章，爲奴請五品，實亂綱紀，不可許。」

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Lu Huaishen and others memorialized: "Guo Qianjin, relying on slight achievement, lightly disregards the imperial regulations; requesting fifth-rank posts for slaves truly disrupts discipline and must not be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Lu Huaishen and others memorialized: "Guo Qianjin, relying on slight merit, lightly disregards the regulations; requesting fifth-rank posts for slaves would truly disrupt discipline and must not be permitted."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以鄫王嗣真爲安北大都護、安撫河東、關內、隴右諸蕃大使，以安北大都護張知運爲之副。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Prince of Zeng Sizhen was made Grand Protector General of the North, Grand Ambassador for Pacifying the various tribes of Hedong, Guannei, and Longyou, with Zhang Zhiyun, Grand Protector General of the North, as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Prince of Zeng Sizhen was made grand protector general of the North and grand ambassador for pacifying the various tribes of Hedong, Guannei, and Longyou, with Zhang Zhiyun, grand protector general of the North, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 陝王嗣升爲安西大都護、安撫河西四鎭諸蕃大使，以安西都護郭虔瓘爲之副。

translations.literal: Prince of Shan Sisheng was made Grand Protector General of Anxi, Grand Ambassador for Pacifying the various tribes of the four garrisons of Hexi, with Guo Qianjin, Protector General of Anxi, as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shan Sisheng was made grand protector general of Anxi and grand ambassador for pacifying the various tribes of the four Hexi garrisons, with Guo Qianjin, protector general of Anxi, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 二王皆不出閣。

translations.literal: Neither prince left the palace precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Neither prince left the palace precinct.

sentences.zh: 諸王遙領節度自此始。

translations.literal: From this time princes holding military governorships at a distance began.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the practice began of princes holding military commands at a distance in name only.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙辰，上幸驪山溫湯。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingchen, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingchen, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃圍松州。

translations.literal: Tibet besieged Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet besieged Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上還宮。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以尚書右丞倪若水爲汴州刺史兼河南採訪使。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Ni Ruoshui, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Prefect of Bianzhou and concurrently Surveillance Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Ni Ruoshui, right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed prefect of Bianzhou and concurrently surveillance commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 上雖欲重都督、刺史，選京官才望者爲之，然當時士大夫猶輕外任。

translations.literal: Although the emperor wished to enhance the status of area commanders and prefects by selecting capital officials of talent and repute for the posts, the literati of the day still looked down on appointments outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor wished to enhance the status of area commanders and prefects by appointing talented and reputable capital officials, the literati of the day still looked down on service outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 揚州採訪使班景倩入爲大理少卿，過大梁，若水餞之行，立望其行塵，久之乃返，謂官屬曰：「班生此行，何異登仙！」

translations.literal: Ban Jingqian, Surveillance Commissioner of Yangzhou, entered the capital as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review; passing through Daliang, Ruoshui saw him off on his journey and stood gazing at the dust of his departing carriage; only after a long while did he return, telling his staff: "Master Ban's journey this time — how is it different from ascending to immortality!"
translations.idiomatic: Ban Jingqian, surveillance commissioner of Yangzhou, entered the capital as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review. Passing through Daliang, Ruoshui saw him off and stood gazing at the dust of his departing carriage; only after a long while did he return and tell his staff: "Master Ban's journey this time — how is it different from ascending to immortality!"

sentences.zh: 癸酉，松州都督孫仁獻襲擊吐蕃於城下，大破之。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Sun Renshi, Area Commander of Songzhou, made a surprise attack on Tibet below the walls and routed them decisively.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Sun Renshi, area commander of Songzhou, launched a surprise attack on the Tibetans below the walls and routed them decisively.

sentences.zh: 上嘗遣宦官詣江南取□鶄、鸂鶒等，欲置苑中，使者所至煩擾。

translations.literal: The emperor once sent eunuchs to the south of the Yangtze to collect □ teal, mandarin ducks, and the like, intending to place them in the imperial park; wherever the envoys went they caused vexation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent eunuchs to the south of the Yangtze to collect red-billed teal, mandarin ducks, and the like for the imperial park; wherever the envoys went they caused trouble.

sentences.zh: 道過汴州，倪若水上言：「今農桑方急，而羅捕禽鳥以供園池之玩，遠自江、嶺，水陸傳送，食爲粱肉。

translations.literal: Passing through Bianzhou, Ni Ruoshui submitted: "Agriculture and sericulture are urgently needed now, yet birds are being netted to supply amusement for gardens and pools, transported from afar from the Yangtze region and the Lingnan, by water and by land, fed on fine grain and meat.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Bianzhou, Ni Ruoshui submitted: "Agriculture and sericulture are urgently needed now, yet birds are being netted for garden and pond amusements, transported from the Yangtze and Lingnan regions by water and land, fed on fine grain and meat.

sentences.zh: 道路觀者，豈不以陛下爲賤人而貴鳥乎？

translations.literal: Would those who watch along the roads not think Your Majesty values birds above men?
translations.idiomatic: Would those who watch along the roads not think Your Majesty values birds above men?

sentences.zh: 陛下方當以鳳凰爲凡鳥，麒麟爲凡獸，況□鶄、鸂鶒，曷足貴也！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to regard the phoenix as an ordinary bird and the qilin as an ordinary beast — how much less are □ teal and mandarin ducks worth esteeming!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought to regard the phoenix as an ordinary bird and the qilin as an ordinary beast — how much less are red-billed teal and mandarin ducks worth esteeming!"

sentences.zh: 上手敕謝若水，賜帛四十段，縱散其鳥。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote an edict apologizing to Ruoshui, bestowed forty bolts of silk, and released the birds to disperse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote an edict apologizing to Ruoshui, bestowed forty bolts of silk, and released the birds.

sentences.zh: 山東蝗復大起，姚崇又命捕之。

translations.literal: Locusts rose again in great numbers in the east; Yao Chong again ordered them captured.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts swarmed again in the east, and Yao Chong again ordered them captured.

sentences.zh: 倪若水謂：「蝗乃天災，非人力所及，宜修德以禳之。

translations.literal: Ni Ruoshui maintained: "Locusts are a heaven-sent disaster, beyond human power; one should cultivate virtue to expel them.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Ruoshui argued: "Locusts are a heaven-sent disaster, beyond human power; one should cultivate virtue to avert them.

sentences.zh: 劉聰時，常捕埋之，爲害益甚。」

translations.literal: In the time of Liu Cong they were often captured and buried, and the harm grew worse."
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Liu Cong they were often captured and buried, and the harm only grew worse."

sentences.zh: 拒御史，不從其命。

translations.literal: He blocked the censor and would not obey the order.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked the censor and refused to obey the order.

sentences.zh: 崇牒若水曰：「劉聰偽主，德不勝妖；

translations.literal: Chong sent Ruoshui a dispatch, saying: "Liu Cong was a usurper; his virtue could not overcome the calamity;
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent Ruoshui a dispatch: "Liu Cong was a usurper; his virtue could not overcome the calamity;

sentences.zh: 今日聖朝，妖不勝德。

translations.literal: Today's sage dynasty — the calamity cannot overcome virtue.
translations.idiomatic: in today's sage dynasty, the calamity cannot overcome virtue.

sentences.zh: 古之良守，蝗不入境。

translations.literal: Ancient worthy magistrates saw locusts not enter their borders.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient worthy magistrates saw locusts not enter their borders.

sentences.zh: 若其修德可免，彼豈無德致然？」

translations.literal: If cultivating virtue could avert them, did they have no virtue that things turned out thus?"
translations.idiomatic: If cultivating virtue could avert them, did those lands have no virtue that things turned out thus?"

sentences.zh: 若水乃不敢違。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruoshui dared not defy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Ruoshui dared not defy.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，甲辰，敕委使者詳察州縣捕蝗勤惰者，各以名聞。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on jiachen, an edict delegated envoys to examine closely the diligence or slackness of prefectures and counties in capturing locusts and report each by name.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on jiachen, an edict delegated envoys to examine closely how diligently or slackly prefectures and counties captured locusts and report each by name.

sentences.zh: 由是連歲蝗災，不至大饑。

translations.literal: Hence, though locust disasters continued year after year, there was no great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Hence, though locust disasters continued year after year, there was no great famine.

sentences.zh: 或言於上曰：「今歲選敘大濫，縣令非才。」

translations.literal: Someone said to the emperor: "This year's selections and promotions are excessively lax — the county magistrates lack talent."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to the emperor: "This year's selections and promotions are excessively lax — the county magistrates lack talent."

sentences.zh: 及入謝，上悉召縣令於宣政殿庭，試以理人策。

translations.literal: When they entered to give thanks, the emperor summoned all county magistrates to the court of the Xuanzheng Hall and tested them with essays on governing people.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered to give thanks, the emperor summoned all county magistrates to the court of the Xuanzheng Hall and tested them with essays on governing people.

sentences.zh: 惟鄄城令韋濟詞理第一，擢爲醴泉令。

translations.literal: Only Wei Ji, Magistrate of Juancheng, ranked first in argument and diction; he was promoted to Magistrate of Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wei Ji, magistrate of Juancheng, ranked first in argument and diction; he was promoted to magistrate of Liquan.

sentences.zh: 餘二百餘人不入第，且令之官；

translations.literal: The remaining two hundred-plus who did not pass were nevertheless ordered to take up their posts;
translations.idiomatic: The remaining two hundred-plus who did not pass were nevertheless ordered to take up their posts;

sentences.zh: 四十五人放歸學問。

translations.literal: forty-five were sent back to pursue their studies.
translations.idiomatic: forty-five were sent back to pursue their studies.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎盧從願左遷豫州剌史，李朝隱左遷滑州刺史。

translations.literal: Lu Congyuan, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was demoted to Prefect of Yuzhou; Li Chaoyin was demoted to Prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congyuan, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, was demoted to prefect of Yuzhou; Li Chaoyin was demoted to prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 從願典選六年，與朝隱皆名稱職。

translations.literal: Congyuan had managed selections for six years; he and Chaoyin were both famed for performing their duties well.
translations.idiomatic: Congyuan had managed selections for six years; he and Chaoyin were both famed for performing their duties well.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗之世，馬載、裴行檢在吏部，最有名，時人稱吏部前有馬、裴，後有盧、李。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the era of Emperor Gaozong, Ma Zai and Pei Xingjian at the Ministry of Personnel were most renowned; people of the time said that before Ma and Pei at the Ministry there were Lu and Li after.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the era of Emperor Gaozong, Ma Zai and Pei Xingjian at the Ministry of Personnel were most renowned; people of the time said that before Ma and Pei at the Ministry, there were Lu and Li after.

sentences.zh: 濟，嗣立之子也。

translations.literal: Ji was the son of Sili.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was the son of Wei Sili.

sentences.zh: 有胡人上言海南多珠翠奇寶，可往營致，因言市舶之利；

translations.literal: A foreigner submitted that south of the sea there were many pearls, jade, and rare treasures that could be sought and obtained, and spoke moreover of the profits of maritime trade;
translations.idiomatic: A foreigner submitted that south of the sea there were many pearls, jade, and rare treasures that could be sought and obtained, and spoke moreover of the profits of maritime trade;

sentences.zh: 又欲往師子國求靈藥及善醫之嫗，置之宮掖。

translations.literal: he also wished to go to Lion Country to seek elixir drugs and a woman skilled in medicine, to place her in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: he also wished to go to Lion Country to seek elixir drugs and a woman skilled in medicine to place in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 上命監察御史楊范臣與胡人偕往求之，范臣從容奏曰：「陛下前年焚珠玉、錦繡，示不復用。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Supervising Censor Yang Fanchen to go with the foreigner to seek these things; Fanchen calmly memorialized: "Your Majesty, the year before last, burned pearls and jade and brocades, showing you would not use them again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Supervising Censor Yang Fanchen to go with the foreigner to seek these things. Fanchen calmly memorialized: "Your Majesty, the year before last you burned pearls, jade, and brocades, showing you would not use them again.

sentences.zh: 今所求者何以異於所焚者乎！

translations.literal: How does what is now sought differ from what was burned!
translations.idiomatic: How does what is now sought differ from what was burned!

sentences.zh: 彼市舶與商賈爭利，殆非王者之體。

translations.literal: That maritime trade competes for profit with merchants — scarcely befits the bearing of a sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Maritime trade competing for profit with merchants scarcely befits the bearing of a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 胡藥之性，中國多不能知；

translations.literal: The properties of foreign drugs — China mostly cannot know them;
translations.idiomatic: The properties of foreign drugs are mostly unknown in China;

sentences.zh: 況於胡嫗，豈宜置之宮掖！

translations.literal: as for a foreign woman, how can she be placed in the inner palace!
translations.idiomatic: as for a foreign woman, how can she be placed in the inner palace!

sentences.zh: 夫御史，天子耳目之官，必有軍國大事，臣雖觸冒炎瘴，死不敢辭。

translations.literal: A censor is an officer of the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; if there were a matter of army and state, your subject though touching miasma and fever would not dare refuse even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: A censor is an officer of the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; if there were a matter of army and state, your subject, though touching miasma and fever, would not refuse even unto death.

sentences.zh: 此特胡人眩惑求媚，無益聖德，竊恐非陛下之意，願熟思之。」

translations.literal: This is merely a foreigner dazzling and currying favor — it benefits not the sage virtue; I privately fear it is not Your Majesty's intent and hope you will consider it deeply."
translations.idiomatic: This is merely a foreigner dazzling and currying favor — it benefits not the sage virtue. I privately fear it is not Your Majesty's intent and hope you will consider it deeply."

sentences.zh: 上遽自引咎，慰諭而罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately took blame upon himself, comforted and instructed him, and dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately took blame upon himself, comforted and instructed him, and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸亥，上皇崩於百福殿。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guihai, the Retired Emperor died in Baifu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guihai, the Retired Emperor died in Baifu Hall.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以上女萬安公主爲女官，欲以追福。

translations.literal: On jisi, the emperor's daughter Princess Wan'an was made a female official, wishing thereby to gain merit for the departed.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the emperor's daughter Princess Wan'an was made a female official, wishing thereby to gain merit for the departed.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，拔曳固斬突厥可汗默啜首來獻。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Bayegu presented the severed head of the Turkic qaghan Mouyuchuo.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the Bayegu presented the severed head of the Turkic qaghan Mouyuchuo.

sentences.zh: 時默啜北擊拔曳固，大破之於獨樂水，恃勝輕歸，不復設備，遇拔曳固迸卒頡質略，自柳林突出，斬之。

translations.literal: At the time Mouyuchuo had marched north against the Bayegu and routed them at Dule River; relying on victory he returned lightly, setting up no defenses; he encountered the Bayegu soldier Jiezhilüe, who burst forth from Willow Grove and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mouyuchuo had marched north against the Bayegu and routed them at Dule River. Relying on victory, he returned lightly without setting up defenses. He encountered the Bayegu soldier Jiezhilüe, who burst forth from Willow Grove and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 時大武軍子將郝靈荃奉使在突厥，頡質略以其首歸之，與偕詣闕，懸其首於廣街。

translations.literal: At the time Sub-lieutenant Hao Lingquan of the Dafu Army was on embassy among the Turks; Jiezhilüe brought the head to him, and together they went to court; the head was hung on the broad street.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sub-lieutenant Hao Lingquan of the Dafu Army was on embassy among the Turks. Jiezhilüe brought the head to him, and together they went to court; the head was hung on the broad street.

sentences.zh: 拔曳固、回紇、同羅、□、僕固五部皆來降，置於大武軍北。

translations.literal: The five tribes — Bayegu, Uighur, Tongluo, □, and Pugu — all came to surrender and were settled north of the Dafu Army.
translations.idiomatic: The five tribes — Bayegu, Uighur, Tongluo, Hun, and Pugu — all came to surrender and were settled north of the Dafu Army.

sentences.zh: 默啜之子小可汗立，骨咄祿之子闕特勒擊殺之，及默啜諸子、親信略盡；

translations.literal: Mouyuchuo's son the Lesser Qaghan took the throne; Kul Tigin, son of Kutlug, struck and killed him, and Mouyuchuo's sons and trusted followers were nearly all destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: Mouyuchuo's son the Lesser Qaghan took the throne; Kul Tigin, son of Kutlug, struck and killed him, and Mouyuchuo's sons and trusted followers were nearly all destroyed;

sentences.zh: 立其兄左賢王默棘連，是爲毘伽可汗，國人謂之「小殺」。

translations.literal: they installed his elder brother, the Left Wise Prince Mojilian, who became the Bilge Qaghan; the people called him "Little Kill."
translations.idiomatic: they installed his elder brother, the Left Wise Prince Mojilian, who became the Bilge Qaghan; the people called him "Little Kill."

sentences.zh: 毘伽以國固讓闕特勒，闕特勒不受；

translations.literal: Bilge firmly offered the state to Kul Tigin, but Kul Tigin would not accept;
translations.idiomatic: Bilge firmly offered the state to Kul Tigin, but Kul Tigin would not accept;

sentences.zh: 乃以爲左賢王，專典兵馬。

translations.literal: he was therefore made Left Wise Prince, with exclusive charge of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: he was therefore made Left Wise Prince, with exclusive charge of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬辰，太常博士陳貞節、蘇獻以太廟七室已滿，請遷中宗神主於別廟，奉睿宗神主祔太廟；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renchen, Court Academicians Chen Zhenjie and Su Xian, because the seven chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were full, requested that Emperor Zhongzong's spirit tablet be moved to a separate temple and Emperor Ruizong's spirit tablet be enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renchen, court academicians Chen Zhenjie and Su Xian, because the seven chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were full, requested that Emperor Zhongzong's spirit tablet be moved to a separate temple and Emperor Ruizong's spirit tablet be enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 又奏遷昭成皇后祔睿宗室，肅明皇后留祀於儀坤廟。

translations.literal: They further memorialized moving Empress Zhaocheng to be enshrined with Ruizong, while Empress Zuming was left for sacrifice at Yikun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: They further memorialized moving Empress Zhaocheng to be enshrined with Ruizong, while Empress Zuming was left for sacrifice at Yikun Temple.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙巳，立中宗廟於太廟之西。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yisi, a temple to Zhongzong was established west of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yisi, a temple to Zhongzong was established west of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 辛未，契丹李失活、奚李大酺帥所部來降。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Li Shihuo of the Khitan and Li Datuo of the Xi led their tribes to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Li Shihuo of the Khitan and Li Datuo of the Xi led their tribes to surrender.

sentences.zh: 制以失活爲松漠郡王、行左金吾大將軍兼松漠都督，因其八部落酋長，拜爲刺史；

translations.literal: An edict made Shihuo Prince of Songmo, acting General of the Left Army of Golden Guards and concurrently Area Commander of Songmo; on account of the eight tribal chieftains, they were appointed prefects;
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Shihuo prince of Songmo, acting general of the Left Army of Golden Guards and concurrently area commander of Songmo; the eight tribal chieftains were appointed prefects;

sentences.zh: 又以將軍薛泰督軍鎭撫之。

translations.literal: General Xue Tai was further sent to oversee troops and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: General Xue Tai was further sent to oversee troops and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 大酺爲饒樂郡王、行右金吾大將軍兼饒樂都督。

translations.literal: Datuo was made Prince of Raole, acting General of the Right Army of Golden Guards and concurrently Area Commander of Raole.
translations.idiomatic: Datuo was made prince of Raole, acting general of the Right Army of Golden Guards and concurrently area commander of Raole.

sentences.zh: 失活，盡忠之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Shihuo was Jinzhong's younger cousin on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Shihuo was the younger cousin of Li Jinzhong on the father's side.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃復請和，上許之。

translations.literal: Tibet again requested peace; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet again requested peace; the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜既死，奚、契丹、拔曳固等諸部皆內附，突騎施蘇祿復自立爲可汗。

translations.literal: After the Turkic Mouyuchuo had died, the Xi, Khitan, Bayegu, and other tribes all submitted inward, and Suluo of the Turgesh again set himself up as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Turkic qaghan Mouyuchuo died, the Xi, Khitan, Bayegu, and other tribes all submitted inward, and Suluo of the Turgesh again set himself up as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 突厥部落多離散，毘伽可汗患之，乃召默啜時牙官暾欲谷，以爲謀主。

translations.literal: Many Turkic tribes were scattered and dispersed; Bilge Qaghan was troubled by this and summoned Tun Yugu, a yabghu from Mouyuchuo's time, to serve as his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Many Turkic tribes were scattered and dispersed; Bilge Qaghan was troubled by this and summoned Tun Yugu, a yabghu from Mouyuchuo's time, to serve as his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷年七十餘，多智略，國人信服之，突厥降戸處河曲者，聞毘伽立，多復叛歸之。

translations.literal: Tun Yugu was over seventy, rich in stratagems; the people trusted him. Among Turkic surrender households settled along the river bend, many hearing Bilge had been enthroned again rebelled and returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tun Yugu was over seventy and rich in stratagems; the people trusted him. Among Turkic surrender households settled along the river bend, many, hearing Bilge had been enthroned, again rebelled and returned to him.

sentences.zh: 并州長史王晙上言：「此屬徒以其國喪亂，故相帥來降；

translations.literal: Wang Jun, Senior Administrator of Bingzhou, submitted: "These people submit only because their state is in turmoil and they lead one another here to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, senior administrator of Bingzhou, submitted: "These people submit only because their state is in turmoil and they lead one another here to surrender;

sentences.zh: 若彼安寧，必復叛去。

translations.literal: If over there they are secure and at peace, they will surely rebel and leave again.
translations.idiomatic: If conditions over there become stable, they will surely rebel and leave again.

sentences.zh: 今置之河曲，此屬桀黠，實難制御，往往不受軍州約束，興兵剽掠；

translations.literal: Now, placing them along the river bend—these people are fierce and cunning and truly hard to control; they often refuse to obey the army commands and prefectures, raise troops, and plunder;
translations.idiomatic: If we leave them along the river bend, these people are fierce and cunning and truly hard to control; they often ignore military and prefectural authority, take up arms, and raid;

sentences.zh: 聞其逃者已多與虜聲問往來，通傳委曲。

translations.literal: I hear that many of their fugitives already exchange messages with the barbarians back and forth, passing along every detail.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that many of their fugitives are already in contact with the barbarians, passing messages back and forth and relaying every detail.

sentences.zh: 乃是畜養此屬使爲間諜，日月滋久，奸詐愈深，窺伺邊隙，將成大患。

translations.literal: This is in effect raising these people to serve as spies; day by month they grow longer, treachery grows deeper, they watch for gaps on the border, and a great calamity will arise.
translations.idiomatic: We are in effect keeping these people here to serve as spies; as time goes on their deceit grows deeper, they watch for openings on the frontier, and a great disaster will result.

sentences.zh: 虜騎南牧，必爲內應，來逼軍州，表裡受敵，雖有韓、彭，不能取勝矣。

translations.literal: When barbarian horsemen drive south to pasture, they will surely serve as inside collaborators, come pressing army commands and prefectures, and be attacked from within and without; even with Han Xin and Peng Yue, victory could not be won.
translations.idiomatic: When barbarian horsemen drive south, they will surely serve as collaborators within our lines, press in on our garrisons and prefectures, and leave us attacked from within and without; even generals like Han Xin and Peng Yue could not win.

sentences.zh: 願以秋、冬之交，大集兵眾，諭以利害，給其資糧，徙之內地。

translations.literal: I wish that at the turn of autumn and winter a great force be assembled, they be instructed in gain and harm, supplied with provisions, and moved into the interior.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that at the turn of autumn and winter we assemble a large force, explain the advantages and dangers to them, supply them with provisions, and relocate them into the interior.

sentences.zh: 二十年外，漸變舊俗，皆成勁兵；

translations.literal: Beyond twenty years, gradually changing their old customs, all will become crack troops;
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty years, as their old ways gradually change, they will all become crack troops;

sentences.zh: 雖一時暫勞，然永久安靖。

translations.literal: Although for a time there will be temporary hardship, yet there will be lasting peace and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Although this will cause temporary hardship, it will bring lasting peace and security.

sentences.zh: 比者守邊將吏及出境使人，多爲諛辭，皆非事實，或雲北虜破滅，或雲降戸妥貼，皆欲自衒其功，非能盡忠徇國。

translations.literal: Recently border garrison officers and envoys sent beyond the frontier mostly use flattery; none of it is factual—some say the northern barbarians are destroyed and wiped out, some say the surrender households are settled and compliant—all wishing to display their own merit, unable to exhaust loyalty and die for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Recently border commanders and envoys sent abroad have mostly spoken flatteringly; none of it is true. Some claim the northern barbarians are destroyed, others that the surrender households are docile—all merely seeking to boast of their achievements rather than serving the state with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 願察斯利口，忽忘遠慮。

translations.literal: I wish you to examine these glib tongues and not suddenly forget far-reaching plans.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty scrutinize these smooth talkers and not forget long-range considerations.

sentences.zh: 議者必曰：『國家向時已嘗置降戸於河曲，皆獲安寧，今何所疑！』

translations.literal: Those who debate will surely say: "The state in former times already once placed surrender households along the river bend, and all obtained peace and security—what is there to doubt now!"
translations.idiomatic: Critics will surely say: "The state has already settled surrender households along the river bend before, and all was peaceful—what is there to doubt now!"

sentences.zh: 此則事同時異，不可不察。

translations.literal: This, then, is the same matter but a different time—it cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: But the circumstances are the same while the times are different; this cannot go unexamined.

sentences.zh: 向者頡利既亡，降者無復異心，故得久安無變。

translations.literal: Formerly, once Jieli was already dead, those who surrendered had no further disloyal hearts, and so long peace without change could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, after Jieli was dead, the surrendering tribes had no further disloyal intent, and so they remained peaceful and unchanged for a long time.

sentences.zh: 今北虜尚存，此屬或畏其威，或懷其惠，或其親屬，豈樂南來！

translations.literal: Now the northern barbarians still exist; these people perhaps fear their might, perhaps cherish their kindness, or perhaps have kin among them—how could they delight in coming south!
translations.idiomatic: Now the northern barbarians still exist; these people may fear their power, may remember their favors, or may have kin among them—why would they be happy to remain in the south!

sentences.zh: 較之彼時，固不侔矣。

translations.literal: Compared with that time, they are indeed not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with that earlier situation, the cases are plainly not the same.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚慮，徙之內地，上也；

translations.literal: By this subject's foolish thinking, moving them into the interior is the upper course;
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, relocating them to the interior is the best policy;

sentences.zh: 多屯士馬，大爲之備，華、夷相參，人勞費廣，次也；

translations.literal: Massing troops and horses and making great preparations, with Chinese and barbarians intermixed, labor and expense broad—this is the middle course;
translations.idiomatic: Massing troops and horses for heavy defenses, with Chinese and barbarians intermixed, causing great labor and expense—this is the second-best option;

sentences.zh: 正如今日，下也。

translations.literal: Precisely like today is the lower course.
translations.idiomatic: Maintaining the present arrangement is the worst option.

sentences.zh: 願審茲三策，擇利而行，縱使因徙逃亡，得者皆爲唐有；

translations.literal: I wish you to examine these three policies, choose what is profitable and act; even if because of relocation some flee, those who are caught will all belong to Tang;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty weigh these three policies and choose the advantageous course; even if some flee during relocation, any who are captured will still belong to Tang;

sentences.zh: 若留至河冰，恐必有變。」

translations.literal: If they are kept until the river freezes, I fear there will surely be a revolt."
translations.idiomatic: If they are left in place until the river freezes, I fear trouble will surely arise."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，未報；

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, but no reply came;
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but no reply came;

sentences.zh: 降戸□夾跌思泰、阿悉爛等果叛。

translations.literal: Among the surrender households, □ Adie Sitai, Asilan, and others did indeed rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Among the surrender households, Adie Sitai, Asilan, and others did indeed rebel.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲辰，命朔方大總管薛訥發兵追討之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the jiachen day, the emperor ordered Grand Commander of Shuofang Xue Ne to dispatch troops to pursue and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the jiachen day, the emperor ordered Xue Ne, grand commander of Shuofang, to dispatch troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 王晙引并州兵西濟河，晝夜兼行，追擊叛者，破之，斬獲三千級。

translations.literal: Wang Jun led Bingzhou troops west across the river, traveling day and night without rest, pursued the rebels, defeated them, and beheaded or captured three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun led Bingzhou troops west across the river, marching day and night, pursued the rebels, defeated them, and killed or captured three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 先是，單于副都護張知運悉收降戸兵仗，令渡河而南，降戸怨怒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Protector-General of the Chanyu Headquarters Zhang Zhiyun had fully collected the surrender households' weapons and armor and ordered them to cross the river southward; the surrender households were resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Zhiyun, vice protector-general of the Chanyu headquarters, had confiscated all the surrender households' weapons and ordered them to cross the river to the south; the surrender households were furious.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞姜晦爲巡邊使，降戸訴無弓矢，不得射獵，晦悉還之；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Jiang Hui served as border inspection envoy; the surrender households complained they had no bows and arrows and could not hunt; Hui fully returned them;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Hui, censor-in-chief, served as border inspection envoy; the surrender households complained that without bows and arrows they could not hunt, and Hui returned them all;

sentences.zh: 降戸得之，遂叛。

translations.literal: The surrender households obtained them and thereupon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Once the surrender households recovered their weapons, they rebelled.

sentences.zh: 張知運不設備，與之戰於青剛嶺，爲虜所擒，欲送突厥；

translations.literal: Zhang Zhiyun made no preparations, fought them at Qinggang Ridge, was captured by the barbarians, and they intended to deliver him to the Turks;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiyun was unprepared; he fought them at Qinggang Ridge, was captured by the rebels, and they intended to hand him over to the Turks;

sentences.zh: 至綏州境，將軍郭知運以朔方兵邀擊之，大破其眾於黑山呼延谷，虜釋張知運而去。

translations.literal: On reaching the border of Suizhou, General Guo Zhiyun with Shuofang troops intercepted and attacked them, greatly defeated their force at Huyan Valley on Black Mountain, and the barbarians released Zhang Zhiyun and left.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the border of Suizhou, General Guo Zhiyun intercepted them with Shuofang troops and routed them at Huyan Valley on Black Mountain; the rebels released Zhang Zhiyun and fled.

sentences.zh: 上以張知運喪師，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Zhang Zhiyun had lost his army, beheaded him as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zhang Zhiyun beheaded as a public example for having lost his command.

sentences.zh: 毘伽可汗既得思泰等，欲南入爲寇。

translations.literal: Once Bilge Qaghan had obtained Sitai and the others, he wished to enter south and make raids.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bilge Qaghan had Sitai and the others in his camp, he wanted to raid south into Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷曰：「唐主英武，民和年豐，未有間隙，不可動也。

translations.literal: Tun Yugu said: "The Tang ruler is heroic and martial, the people are harmonious and the years abundant; there is no opening—one cannot act.
translations.idiomatic: Tun Yugu said: "The Tang emperor is heroic and capable, the people are at peace and the harvests are good; there is no opening to exploit—we must not move.

sentences.zh: 我眾新集，力尚疲羸，且當息養數年，始可觀變而舉。」

translations.literal: Our multitude is newly gathered, strength is still weary and weak; for now we should rest and nurture for several years, and only then observe changes and act."
translations.idiomatic: Our forces are newly assembled and still weak; we should rest and recover for several years before watching for changes and striking."

sentences.zh: 毘伽又欲築城，並立寺觀，暾欲谷曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Bilge again wished to build walled cities and also erect temples and monasteries; Tun Yugu said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Bilge also wanted to build walled cities and erect temples and monasteries; Tun Yugu said: "That must not be done.

sentences.zh: 突厥人徒稀少，不及唐家百分之一，所以能與爲敵者，正以逐水草，居處無常，射獵爲業，人皆習武，強則進兵抄掠，弱則竄伏山林。

translations.literal: Turkic people are few in number, not reaching one percent of the Tang house; the reason we can be their enemy is precisely that we follow water and grass, dwell without fixed abode, take hunting as our livelihood, all men practice arms—when strong we advance troops to raid and plunder, when weak we hide in mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks are few in number, less than one percent of Tang's population; the reason we can stand as their enemy is precisely that we follow pasture and water, live without fixed settlements, and hunt for a living. All our men are trained in arms—when strong we advance to raid, when weak we hide in the mountains and forests.

sentences.zh: 唐兵雖多，無所施用。

translations.literal: Although Tang troops are many, there is nowhere to apply them.
translations.idiomatic: However many Tang troops they send, there is no way to use them effectively against us.

sentences.zh: 若築城而居，變更舊俗，一朝失利，必爲所滅。

translations.literal: If we build cities and dwell in them, changing our old customs, once we suffer defeat we will surely be destroyed by them.
translations.idiomatic: If we settle in walled cities and abandon our old ways, the moment we suffer a setback we will surely be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 釋、老之法，教人仁弱，非用武爭勝之術，不可崇也。」

translations.literal: The laws of Buddhism and Daoism teach people benevolence and weakness; they are not arts for using force to struggle for victory—they must not be honored."
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist and Daoist teachings cultivate gentleness and weakness; they are not methods for winning by force of arms and must not be promoted."

sentences.zh: 毘伽乃止。

translations.literal: Bilge thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bilge then abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 庚午，葬大聖皇帝於橋陵，廟號睿宗。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day, the Great Sage Emperor was buried at Qiao Mausoleum; his temple name was Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day, the Great Sage Emperor was buried at Qiao Mausoleum and given the temple name Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李傑護橋陵作，判官王旭犯贓，傑按之，反爲所構，左遷衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Jie oversaw construction at Qiao Mausoleum; judicial officer Wang Xu committed bribery; Jie investigated him but was in turn framed by him and was demoted to prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jie, censor-in-chief, oversaw construction at Qiao Mausoleum; his judicial officer Wang Xu took bribes, and when Jie investigated him, Wang framed him in return; Jie was demoted to prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己卯，黃門監盧懷慎疾亟，上表薦宋璟、李傑、李朝隱、盧從願並明時重器，所坐者小，所棄者大，望垂矜錄；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the jimao day, Supervisor of the Yellow Gate Lu Huaiqian was gravely ill; he submitted a memorial recommending Song Jing, Li Jie, Li Chaoyin, and Lu Congyuan as all heavy vessels of a bright age—the offenses for which they were punished were small, what was cast aside was great; he hoped for compassionate enrollment;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the jimao day, Lu Huaiqian, supervisor of the Yellow Gate, was gravely ill; he submitted a memorial recommending Song Jing, Li Jie, Li Chaoyin, and Lu Congyuan as men of great talent for the age, arguing that the faults for which they had been punished were minor while what the court had lost was great, and asking that they be shown mercy and restored;

sentences.zh: 上深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fully accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 乙未，薨。

translations.literal: On the yimao day, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day, he died.

sentences.zh: 家無餘蓄，惟一老蒼頭，請自鬻以辦喪事。

translations.literal: His household had no surplus stores; there was only one old manservant, who asked to sell himself to arrange the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: His household had no savings; he left only one elderly manservant, who offered to sell himself to pay for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以尚書左丞源乾曜爲黃門侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Yuan Qianyao was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, Yuan Qianyao, left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed vice director of the Yellow Gate and associate director of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 姚崇無居第，寓居罔極寺，以病痁謁告。

translations.literal: Yao Chong had no residence; he lodged at Wuji Temple and requested leave on account of malarial illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong had no house of his own and was staying at Wuji Temple, where he requested sick leave for malaria.

sentences.zh: 上遣使問飲食起居狀，日數十輩。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to inquire about his food, drink, and daily condition—several tens each day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to inquire after his diet and daily condition, dozens each day.

sentences.zh: 源乾曜奏事或稱旨，上輒曰：「此必姚宗之謀也。」

translations.literal: When Yuan Qianyao reported on affairs and sometimes hit the mark, the emperor would say: "This must be Yao Zongzhi's plan."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Qianyao reported on affairs and the emperor was pleased, he would say: "This must be Yao Yuanzhi's counsel."

sentences.zh: 或不稱旨，輒曰：「何不與姚崇議之！」

translations.literal: Or when it did not hit the mark, he would say: "Why not discuss it with Yao Chong!"
translations.idiomatic: When he was displeased, he would say: "Why did you not consult Yao Chong!"

sentences.zh: 乾曜常謝實然。

translations.literal: Qianyao often thanked him with embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao would often apologize in embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 每有大事，上常令乾曜就寺問崇。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a great matter, the emperor often had Qianyao go to the temple to ask Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a major matter arose, the emperor would send Qianyao to the temple to consult Chong.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，乾曜請遷崇於四方館，仍聽家人入侍疾；

translations.literal: On the guimao day, Qianyao requested that Chong be moved to the Foreign Guests Pavilion and that his family still be allowed to enter and attend his illness;
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, Qianyao asked that Chong be moved to the Foreign Guests Pavilion and that his family be allowed to attend him there;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 崇以四方館有簿書，非病者所宜外，固辭。

translations.literal: Chong, because the Foreign Guests Pavilion had registers and documents and was not suitable for the ill besides, firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Chong firmly declined, saying the Foreign Guests Pavilion held official records and was no place for a sick man.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「設四方館，爲官吏也；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Foreign Guests Pavilion was established for officials;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Foreign Guests Pavilion was built for officials;

sentences.zh: 使卿居之，爲社稷也。

translations.literal: having you dwell there is for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: having you stay there is for the sake of the state.

sentences.zh: 恨不可使卿居禁中耳，此何足辭！」

translations.literal: I regret that I cannot have you dwell within the Forbidden Inner Palace—what is there in this worth declining!"
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that I cannot have you stay inside the palace itself—why refuse this!"

sentences.zh: 崇子光祿少卿彝、宗正少卿異，廣通賓客，頗受饋遺，爲時所譏。

translations.literal: Chong's sons, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Yi and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Yi, widely received guests and quite accepted gifts; they were ridiculed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong's sons, Yi, vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Yi, vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, entertained many guests and accepted numerous gifts, drawing public criticism.

sentences.zh: 主書趙誨爲崇所親信，受胡人賂，事覺，上親鞫問，下獄當死。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhao Hui was trusted by Chong; he accepted bribes from barbarians; when the matter came to light, the emperor personally interrogated him; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hui, a chief clerk whom Chong trusted, took bribes from barbarians; when the affair came to light, the emperor personally interrogated him, and he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 崇復營救，上由是不悅。

translations.literal: Chong again worked to rescue him; the emperor was thereby displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Chong again intervened on his behalf, and the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會曲赦京城，敕特標誨名，杖之一百，流嶺南。

translations.literal: It happened that there was a partial amnesty in the capital; the edict specially listed Hui's name, gave him one hundred blows with the staff, and exiled him to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When a partial amnesty was issued for the capital, the edict specifically named Hui, sentenced him to one hundred strokes of the staff, and exiled him to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 崇由是憂懼，數請避相位，薦廣州都督宋璟自代。

translations.literal: Chong was thereby anxious and fearful; he repeatedly asked to step aside from the chancellor's post and recommended Regional Commander of Guangzhou Song Jing to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chong grew anxious and repeatedly asked to resign the chancellorship, recommending Song Jing, regional commander of Guangzhou, as his successor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，上將幸東都，以璟爲刑部尚書、西京留守，令馳驛詣闕，遣內侍、將軍楊思勖迎之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital; he made Jing Minister of Justice and Western Capital Regent, ordered him to come posthaste to court by relay, and sent Inner Attendant and General Yang Sixun to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, as the emperor prepared to visit the Eastern Capital, he appointed Song Jing minister of justice and regent of the Western Capital, ordered him to come to court by relay post, and sent the inner attendant and general Yang Sixun to meet him.

sentences.zh: 璟風度凝遠，人莫測其際，在塗竟不與思勖交言。

translations.literal: Jing's bearing was grave and distant; people could not fathom his depths; on the road he ultimately did not exchange words with Sixun.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing's manner was reserved and distant, and no one could read him; on the journey he never exchanged a word with Sixun.

sentences.zh: 思勖素貴幸，歸，訴於上，上嗟歎良久，益重璟。

translations.literal: Sixun was by nature honored and favored; on returning he complained to the emperor; the emperor sighed for a long while and valued Jing all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun, who was accustomed to high favor, complained to the emperor on his return; the emperor sighed at length and respected Song Jing all the more.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，上幸驪山溫湯；

translations.literal: On the bingchen day, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 乙丑，還宮。

translations.literal: On the yichou day, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己亥，姚崇罷爲開府儀同三司，源乾曜罷爲京兆尹、西京留守，以刑部尚書宋璟守吏部尚書兼黃門監，紫微侍郎蘇頲同平章事。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the jihai day, Yao Chong was dismissed and made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Same Three Ranks as the Three Excellencies; Yuan Qianyao was dismissed and made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and Western Capital Regent; Minister of Justice Song Jing was made acting Minister of Personnel and concurrently Supervisor of the Yellow Gate; Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Su Ting was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the jihai day, Yao Chong was removed as chief minister and made grand master of splendid happiness with ceremonial rank equal to the three excellencies; Yuan Qianyao was removed and made metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and regent of the Western Capital; Song Jing, minister of justice, was appointed acting minister of personnel and supervisor of the Yellow Gate; and Su Ting, vice director of the Palace Secretariat, was made associate director of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 璟爲相，務在擇人，隨材授任，使百官各稱其積；

translations.literal: Jing as chancellor devoted himself to selecting men, assigning duties according to talent, and making the hundred officials each fit their posts;
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Song Jing focused on selecting the right men, assigning posts according to talent, and ensuring that every official was suited to his duties;

sentences.zh: 刑賞無私，敢犯顏正諫。

translations.literal: Punishments and rewards were without partiality; he dared to oppose the countenance with straight remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments were impartial, and he dared to remonstrate frankly even when the emperor's face darkened.

sentences.zh: 上甚敬憚之，雖不合意，亦曲從之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly respected and feared him; even when it did not accord with his intent, he still bent to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held him in deep respect and awe; even when he disagreed, he would yield to Song Jing.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜自則天世爲中國患，朝廷旰食，傾天下之力不能克；

translations.literal: The Turk Moquluo since Empress Wu's age had been a calamity to China; the court ate late meals, poured out the empire's strength, and could not overcome him;
translations.idiomatic: The Turk Mo-ch'o had been a scourge to China since Empress Wu's reign; the court worked late into the evening and mobilized the empire's full strength without defeating him;

sentences.zh: 郝靈荃得其首，自謂不世之功。

translations.literal: Hao Lingquan obtained his head and considered it an unworldly achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao Lingquan took his head, he regarded it as a once-in-a-lifetime achievement.

sentences.zh: 璟以天子好武功，恐好事者競生心徼倖，痛抑其賞，逾年始授郎將；

translations.literal: Jing, because the Son of Heaven loved military achievement, feared that those eager for action would compete in giving rise to hearts of opportunism; he severely suppressed his reward, and only after more than a year was he granted the post of commandant;
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing, fearing that the emperor's love of martial glory would encourage others to seek similar windfalls, deliberately withheld Hao's reward; only after more than a year was he appointed a commandant;

sentences.zh: 靈荃慟哭而死。

translations.literal: Lingquan wailed and wept and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Lingquan died of grief.

sentences.zh: 璟與蘇頲相得甚厚，頲遇事多讓於璟，頲每論事則頲爲之助。

translations.literal: Jing and Su Ting got along very deeply; when Ting encountered matters he often yielded to Jing; whenever Ting discussed affairs, Ting would assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and Su Ting were on very close terms; Su Ting often deferred to Song Jing in handling affairs, and whenever Song Jing took up a matter, Su Ting would support him.

sentences.zh: 璟嘗謂人曰：「吾與蘇氏父子皆同居相府，僕射寬厚，誠爲國器，然獻可替否，吏事精敏，則黃門過其父矣。」

translations.literal: Jing once said to people: "Both Su Ting and I have served together in the chancellery with father and son; the Vice Director is generous and broad, truly a vessel of state, yet in offering approval where appropriate and rejection where not, and in the precision of administrative affairs, the Yellow Gate Director surpasses his father."
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing once said to others: "Su Ting and I have both served in the chancellery together with his father; the vice director is generous and truly a pillar of state, but in weighing what to approve and what to reject, and in the precision of administrative work, the Yellow Gate director surpasses his father."

sentences.zh: 姚、宋相繼爲相，崇善應變成務，璟善守法持正；

translations.literal: Yao and Song succeeded one another as chancellor; Chong was good at adapting and completing tasks, Jing was good at upholding law and holding to rectitude;
