translations.idiomatic: Yao and Song served as chief ministers in succession; Yao Chong excelled at adapting to circumstances and getting things done, while Song Jing excelled at upholding the law and maintaining integrity;

sentences.zh: 二人志操不同，然協心輔佐，使賦役寬平，刑罰清省，百姓富遮。

translations.literal: The two men's aspirations and conduct differed, yet they cooperated in heart to assist, making levies and corvée broad and even, punishments clear and reduced, and the common people wealthy and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Their temperaments differed, yet they worked in concert as ministers, keeping taxes and corvée moderate, punishments fair and sparing, and the people prosperous.

sentences.zh: 唐世賢相，前稱房、杜，後稱姚、宋，他人莫得比焉。

translations.literal: Among Tang's worthy chancellors, earlier they were called Fang and Du, later Yao and Song; others could not be compared to them.
translations.idiomatic: Among Tang's great ministers, the early age was praised for Fang and Du, the later age for Yao and Song; no others could compare.

sentences.zh: 二人每進見，上輒爲之起，去則臨軒送之。

translations.literal: Whenever the two men came to audience, the emperor would rise for them; when they left, he would see them off from the front of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the two came to audience, the emperor would rise for them, and when they left he would see them off from the front of the hall.

sentences.zh: 及李林甫爲相，雖寵任過於姚、宋，然禮遇殊卑薄矣。

translations.literal: When Li Linfu became chancellor, although favor and appointment surpassed Yao and Song, yet the courtesy shown was especially low and thin.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Linfu became chief minister, although his favor exceeded what Yao and Song had enjoyed, the courtesy shown him was far less.

sentences.zh: 紫微舍人高仲舒博通典籍，齊澣練習時務，姚、宋每坐二人以質所疑，既而歎曰：「欲知古，問高群，欲知今，問齊君，可以無缺政矣。」

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Attendant Gao Zhongshu was broadly versed in the classics and histories; Qi Huan was practiced in current affairs; Yao and Song often seated the two men to question what they doubted, and afterward sighed and said: "To know antiquity, ask the Gao group; to know the present, ask Master Qi—one can be without deficient governance."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhongshu, an attendant of the Palace Secretariat, was deeply learned in the classics, and Qi Huan was well versed in current affairs; Yao and Song often seated the two men to consult them on doubtful points, and then sighed: "To understand antiquity, ask Gao; to understand the present, ask Qi—with them, governance need lack nothing."

sentences.zh: 辛丑，罷十道按察使。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day, the ten-circuit inspection commissioners were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day, the ten-circuit inspection commissioners were abolished.

sentences.zh: 舊制，六品以下官皆委尚書省奏擬。

translations.literal: Under the old system, officials of the sixth rank and below were all entrusted to the Department of State Affairs for memorial nomination.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, all officials of the sixth rank and below were nominated by the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是歲，始制員外郎、御史、起居、遺、補不擬。

translations.literal: This year, it was first decreed that externals, censors, diarists, remonstrators, and supplements would not be nominated.
translations.idiomatic: That year, a rule was first established that externals, censors, diarists, remonstrators, and supplements would no longer be subject to ministerial nomination.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯，太廟四室壞，上素服避正殿。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the guimao day, four chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple collapsed; the emperor wore plain robes and avoided the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the guimao day, four chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple collapsed; the emperor wore mourning dress and avoided the main hall.

sentences.zh: 時上將幸東都，以問宋璟、蘇頲，對曰：「陛下三年之制未終，遽爾行幸，恐未契天心，災異爲戒；

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital; he asked Song Jing and Su Ting; they replied: "Your Majesty's three-year mourning is not yet finished; hastily making this journey—I fear it may not accord with Heaven's heart; calamities and anomalies serve as warnings;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital and consulted Song Jing and Su Ting; they replied: "Your Majesty's three-year mourning period is not yet complete; to travel so soon may fail to accord with Heaven's will, and this disaster is a warning;

sentences.zh: 願且停車駕。」

translations.literal: I wish you would for now halt the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: we ask that Your Majesty postpone the journey."

sentences.zh: 又問姚崇，對曰：「太廟屋材，皆苻堅時物，歲久朽腐而壞，適與行期相會，何足異也！

translations.literal: He again asked Yao Chong; he replied: "The timber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple was all material from Fu Jian's time; after years it rotted and collapsed—this just happened to coincide with the date of travel; what is there strange in it!
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Yao Chong, who replied: "The timber in the Imperial Ancestral Temple dates from Fu Jian's time; after long years it rotted and gave way—this simply coincided with your travel plans; there is nothing remarkable in that!

sentences.zh: 且王者以四海爲家，陛下以關中不稔幸東都，百司供擬已備，不可失信；

translations.literal: Moreover, a king takes the four seas as his home; Your Majesty, because Guanzhong's harvest was poor, visits the Eastern Capital; the hundred offices' provisions are already prepared—it cannot lose faith;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a ruler takes all under Heaven as his home; Your Majesty is visiting the Eastern Capital because the Guanzhong harvest was poor, and the various offices have already made preparations—it would be wrong to break faith;

sentences.zh: 但應遷神主於太極殿，更修太廟，如期自行耳。」

translations.literal: One need only move the spirit tablets to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, rebuild the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and proceed on schedule—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: You need only move the spirit tablets to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, rebuild the temple, and depart on schedule."

sentences.zh: 上大喜，從之，賜崇絹二百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, followed this, and bestowed on Chong two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, followed his advice, and rewarded Chong with two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 己酉，上行享禮於太極殿，命姚崇五日一朝，仍入閣供奉，恩禮更厚，有大政輒訪焉。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day, the emperor performed the offering rite at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, ordered Yao Chong to attend court once every five days, and still enter the pavilion to serve; favor and courtesy grew thicker, and whenever there was a great policy he would consult him.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day, the emperor performed the offering rite at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, ordered Yao Chong to attend court every five days, and continued to receive him in the inner pavilion; his honors grew even greater, and the emperor consulted him on every major policy matter.

sentences.zh: 右散騎常侍褚無量上言：「隋文帝富有天下，遷都之日，豈取苻氏舊材以立太廟乎？

translations.literal: Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse Chu Wuliang submitted: "When Emperor Wen of Sui possessed all under Heaven, on the day of moving the capital, would he have taken Fu clan old timber to establish the Imperial Ancestral Temple?
translations.idiomatic: Chu Wuliang, right regular attendant of the Palace Horse, submitted: "When Emperor Wen of Sui ruled the empire, on the day he moved the capital, would he have used old Fu-clan timber to build the Imperial Ancestral Temple?

sentences.zh: 此特諛臣之言耳。

translations.literal: This is merely the words of a flatterer.
translations.idiomatic: That is merely the talk of a flatterer.

sentences.zh: 願陛下克謹天戒，訥忠諫，遠諂諛。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty earnestly heed Heaven's warnings, accept loyal remonstrance, and keep flattery and sycophancy at a distance."
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty earnestly heed Heaven's warnings, accept loyal counsel, and keep sycophants at arm's length."

sentences.zh: 上弗聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，行幸東都。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day, the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day, the emperor set out for the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 達崤谷，道隘不治；

translations.literal: When he reached Xiaogu Pass, the road was narrow and had not been repaired;
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaogu Pass the road was narrow and unmaintained;

sentences.zh: 上欲免河南尹及知頓使官，宋璟諫曰：「陛下方事巡幸，今以此罪二臣，臣恐將來民受其弊。」

translations.literal: the emperor wished to dismiss the Henan governor and the staging-office commissioners; Song Jing remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty is just now undertaking an imperial tour; if you punish these two officials for this offense, I fear that in the future the people will suffer the harm."
translations.idiomatic: the emperor wished to dismiss the governor of Henan and the staging commissioners. Song Jing remonstrated: "Your Majesty is on tour; to punish these two officials for this now, I fear the people will suffer in future."

sentences.zh: 上遽命釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered them released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered their release.

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「陛下罪之，以臣言而免之，是臣代陛下受德也；

translations.literal: Song Jing said: "Your Majesty punished them, yet because of my words you pardoned them—this is my receiving the credit on Your Majesty's behalf;
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing said: "Your Majesty condemned them, then pardoned them at my word—that means I have taken the credit that should be Yours;

sentences.zh: 請令待罪朝堂而後赦之。」

translations.literal: I ask that they be made to await punishment in the court hall, and only then be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: let them stand awaiting judgment in the hall of audience, and pardon them only afterward."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲戌，至東都，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the jiaxu day, he arrived at the Eastern Capital and proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the jiaxu day, he reached the Eastern Capital and issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 奚、契丹既內附，貝州刺史宋慶禮建議，請復營州。

translations.literal: The Xi and Khitan having submitted and come within the borders, Pei Prefecture governor Song Qingli proposed restoring Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Xi and Khitan had submitted, Song Qingli, governor of Pei Prefecture, proposed restoring Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚戌，制復置營州都督於柳城，兼平盧軍使，管內州縣鎭戍皆如其舊；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the gengxu day, by edict Ying Prefecture Protectorate was reestablished at Liucheng, concurrently serving as Pinglu Army commissioner; prefectures, counties, garrison posts, and fortifications within its jurisdiction were all restored as before;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the gengxu day, an edict reestablished the Yingzhou Protectorate at Liucheng, with the concurrent post of Pinglu Army commissioner; all counties, garrisons, and posts within its jurisdiction were restored as before;

sentences.zh: 以太子詹事姜師度爲營田、支度使，與慶禮等築之，三旬而畢。

translations.literal: the crown prince's household steward Jiang Shidu was made commissioner of military colonies and logistics, and together with Qingli and others built it; in thirty days it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shidu, chamberlain of the heir apparent, was appointed commissioner of military colonies and logistics; he and Qingli and the others completed construction in thirty days.

sentences.zh: 慶禮清勤嚴肅，開屯田八十餘所，招安流散，數年之間，倉廩充實，市邑浸繁。

translations.literal: Qingli was upright, diligent, and strict; he opened more than eighty military colonies, gathered and settled dispersed refugees, and within several years the granaries were full and market towns steadily multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli was upright, diligent, and disciplined; he established more than eighty military colonies, resettled refugees, and within a few years the granaries were filled and the towns grew steadily.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲戌，賜奚王李大酺妃辛氏號固安公主。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the jiaxu day, the consort of Xi king Li Dapo, Lady Xin, was granted the title Princess Guo'an.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the jiaxu day, Lady Xin, consort of Li Dapo, king of the Xi, was given the title Princess Guo'an.

sentences.zh: 己丑，皇子嗣一卒，追立爲夏王，謚曰悼。

translations.literal: On the jichou day, the prince Siyi died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xia, with posthumous name Dao.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day, Prince Siyi died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xia, posthumous name Dao.

sentences.zh: 嗣一母武惠妃，攸止之女也。

translations.literal: Siyi's mother was Consort Wu Hui, daughter of Wu Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Consort Wu Hui, daughter of Wu Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 突騎施酋長左羽林大將軍蘇祿部眾浸強，雖職貢不乏，陰有窺邊之志。

translations.literal: The Turgesh chieftain, Left Guard General of the Feathered Forest Su Lu—his tribesmen gradually growing stronger—though tribute was not lacking, secretly he harbored designs to encroach upon the border.
translations.idiomatic: Su Lu, chieftain of the Turgesh and Left Guard General of the Feathered Forest, was growing stronger; though tribute continued unbroken, he secretly harbored ambitions against the frontier.

sentences.zh: 五月，十姓可汗阿史那獻欲發葛邏祿兵擊之，上不許。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the On Ok Khan Ashina Xian wished to mobilize Karluk troops to strike him; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Ashina Xian, khan of the Ten Surnames, asked to mobilize Karluk troops against him; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 初，上微時，與太常卿姜皎親善。

translations.literal: Previously, when the emperor was still in low station, he was close with Director of Imperial Sacrifices Jiang Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while the emperor was still a private gentleman, he was close to Jiang Jiao, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 及誅竇懷貞等，皎預有功。

translations.literal: When Dou Huaiyue and others were executed, Jiao shared in the merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Huaiyue and his associates were eliminated, Jiao had played a part in the achievement.

sentences.zh: 由是寵遇群臣莫及，常出入臥內，與后妃連榻宴飲，賞賜不可勝紀。

translations.literal: From this his favor surpassed all officials; he regularly entered and left the sleeping quarters, shared couches for feasting and drinking with the consorts, and rewards beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From then on no courtier enjoyed greater favor; he came and went freely in the inner chambers, feasted and drank with the imperial consorts on shared couches, and received rewards too many to count.

sentences.zh: 弟晦，亦以皎故累遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hui, also because of Jiao, was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Hui, likewise through Jiao's influence, rose to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宋璟言皎兄弟權寵太盛，非所以安之，上亦以爲然。

translations.literal: Song Jing said the Jiao brothers' power and favor were too great—not the way to keep them secure—and the emperor also thought so.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing warned that the Jiao brothers had grown too powerful—a danger to their own safety—and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚子，以晦爲宗正卿，因下制曰：「西漢諸將，以權貴不全；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the gengzi day, Hui was made director of the Imperial Clan Court, and an edict was issued, stating: "The generals of Western Han, because of power and nobility did not come to a good end;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the gengzi day, Hui was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court, and an edict declared: "The generals of Western Han, once elevated to power and rank, rarely died in peace;

sentences.zh: 南陽故人，以優閒自保。

translations.literal: the old friends of Nanyang, through leisured ease preserved themselves.
translations.idiomatic: the old companions at Nanyang kept themselves safe through a life of ease.

sentences.zh: 皎宜放歸田園，散官、勳、封皆如故。」

translations.literal: Jiao should be released to return to his estate; his honorary offices, orders of merit, and enfeoffments shall all remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: Jiao should be sent back to his country estate; his honorary titles, orders of merit, and fief shall remain unchanged."

sentences.zh: 壬寅，隴右節度使郭知運大破吐蕃於九曲。

translations.literal: On the renyin day, Longyou military commissioner Guo Zhiyun heavily defeated the Tibetans at Nine Bends.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day, Guo Zhiyun, military commissioner of Longyou, won a great victory over the Tibetans at Nine Bends.

sentences.zh: 安西副大都護湯嘉惠奏突騎施引大食、吐蕃，謀取四鎭，圍缽換及大石城，已發三姓葛邏祿兵與阿史那獻擊之。

translations.literal: Acting Protector-General of Anxi Tang Jiahui memorialized that the Turgesh had brought in the Arabs and Tibetans, plotting to seize the Four Garrisons, and had besieged Bolü and Tashkent; he had already dispatched Three Surname Karluk troops together with Ashina Xian to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jiahui, acting protector-general of Anxi, reported that the Turgesh had allied with the Arabs and Tibetans, planned to seize the Four Garrisons, and were besieging Ferghana and Tashkent; he had already mobilized Karluk forces from the Three Surnames together with Ashina Xian to counter them.

sentences.zh: 并州長史張嘉貞上言：「突厥九姓新降者，散居太原以北，請宿重兵以鎭之。」

translations.literal: Bingzhou chief administrator Zhang Jiazhen submitted: "The newly surrendered Nine Surnames of the Turks, dispersed north of Taiyuan—I ask that heavy troops be stationed to pacify them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen, chief administrator of Bingzhou, submitted: "The newly surrendered Nine Surnames of the Turks are scattered north of Taiyuan; I ask that a strong garrison be posted to keep them in check."

sentences.zh: 辛酉，置天兵軍於并州，集兵八萬，以嘉貞爲天兵軍大使。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day, the Heavenly Army was established at Bingzhou, gathering eighty thousand troops; Jiazhen was made commissioner of the Heavenly Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day, the Heavenly Army was established at Bingzhou with a force of eighty thousand, and Jiazhen was appointed its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿王仁惠等奏則天立明堂不合古制；

translations.literal: Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Renhui and others memorialized that Empress Wu's establishment of the Bright Hall did not accord with ancient institutions;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renhui, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and others memorialized that the Bright Hall built under Empress Wu violated ancient precedent;

sentences.zh: 又，明堂尚質，而窮極奢侈，密邇宮掖，人神雜擾。

translations.literal: moreover, the Bright Hall should value simplicity, yet it was pushed to extreme extravagance, stood close beside the palace quarters, and human and divine affairs were thrown into confusion together.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, the Bright Hall ought to embody plainness, yet Wu's hall was extravagantly built hard by the palace, mingling human and sacred rites in disorder.

sentences.zh: 甲子，制復以明堂爲乾元殿，冬至、元日受朝賀，季秋大享，復就圜丘。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day, by edict the Bright Hall was again made the Qianyuan Hall; at the winter solstice and New Year's Day court audiences were received, and the great autumn offering was again performed at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day, an edict restored the Bright Hall as the Qianyuan Hall: the winter-solstice and New Year audiences would be held there, while the great autumn offering would again be performed at the Round Mound Altar.

sentences.zh: 九月，中書、門下省及侍中皆復舊名。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Secretariat, the Chancellery, and the title of Palace Attendant were all restored to their former names.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the Secretariat, the Chancellery, and the post of Palace Attendant all reverted to their former titles.

sentences.zh: 貞觀之制，中書、門下及三品官入奏事，必使諫官、史官隨之，有失則匡正，美惡必記之；

translations.literal: Under the Zhenguan system, when Secretariat and Chancellery officials and third-rank ministers entered to report affairs, remonstrating officers and recording officers were required to accompany them; if there was error it was corrected, and good and bad were invariably recorded;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenguan system, when ministers of the Secretariat and Chancellery and officials of the third rank came to report business, remonstrating officers and historiographers had to accompany them; errors were corrected on the spot, and deeds good or ill were duly recorded;

sentences.zh: 諸司皆於正牙奏事，御史彈百官，服豸冠，對仗讀彈文；

translations.literal: all offices reported affairs at the main audience hall; censors impeached officials wearing the xie hat, reading impeachment documents facing the imperial guard;
translations.idiomatic: all departments reported at the main audience hall; censors impeaching officials wore the xie crown and read their impeachments before the imperial guard ranks;

sentences.zh: 故大臣不得專君而小臣不得爲讒慝。

translations.literal: therefore great ministers could not monopolize the ruler, and lesser officials could not practice slander and malice.
translations.idiomatic: thus senior ministers could not monopolize access to the throne, and junior officials could not traffic in slander.

sentences.zh: 及許敬宗、李義府用事，政多私僻，奏事官多俟仗下，於御坐前屏左右密奏，監奏御史及待制官遠立以俟其退；

translations.literal: When Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu held power, government was largely private and irregular; memorializing officials mostly waited until the guard ranks were dismissed, then at the imperial seat screened away attendants and reported in secret, while supervising censors and awaiting-appointment officials stood far off waiting for their withdrawal;
translations.idiomatic: Once Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu dominated affairs, government grew secretive; officials reporting business often waited until the guard ranks were dismissed, then petitioned privately before the throne with attendants excluded, while supervising censors and awaiting-appointment officers stood far off until they withdrew;

sentences.zh: 諫官、史官皆隨仗出，仗下後事，不復預聞。

translations.literal: remonstrating officers and recording officers all departed with the guard ranks; after the ranks were dismissed, affairs were no longer heard in advance.
translations.idiomatic: remonstrating officers and historiographers left with the guard formation; affairs conducted after dismissal of the ranks they no longer heard of.

sentences.zh: 武後以法制群下，諫官、御史得以風聞言事，自御史大夫至監察得互相彈奏，率以險詖相傾覆。

translations.literal: Empress Wu used law to control the officials below; remonstrating officers and censors could speak on hearsay, and from the censor-in-chief down to investigating censors they could impeach one another, generally overthrowing one another through vicious slander.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu governed her officials through intimidation; censors and remonstrators could denounce others on mere rumor, and censors of every rank impeached one another, usually seeking to destroy rivals with vicious charges.

sentences.zh: 及宋璟爲相，欲復貞觀之政，戊申，制：「自今事非的須秘密者，皆令對仗奏聞，史官自依故事。」

translations.literal: When Song Jing became chancellor, wishing to restore Zhenguan government, on the wushen day an edict stated: "From now on, in matters not requiring secrecy, all are to report before the guard ranks; recording officers shall follow the old precedent."
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jing became chancellor and sought to restore Zhenguan practice, an edict on the wushen day declared: "Hereafter, except where secrecy is truly required, all business shall be reported before the guard ranks; historiographers shall follow established custom."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸酉，伊闕人孫平子上言：「《春秋》譏魯躋僖公；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the guiyou day, Sun Pingzi of Yique submitted: "The Spring and Autumn Annals censures Lu for elevating Duke Xi;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the guiyou day, Sun Pingzi of Yique submitted: "The Spring and Autumn Annals rebukes Lu for elevating Duke Xi above his place;

sentences.zh: 今遷中宗於別廟而祀睿宗，正與魯同。

translations.literal: now moving Emperor Zhongzong to a separate temple while sacrificing to Emperor Ruizong is exactly the same as Lu.
translations.idiomatic: moving Emperor Zhongzong to a separate shrine while honoring Emperor Ruizong in the main temple repeats Lu's error.

sentences.zh: 兄臣於弟，猶不可躋，況弟臣于兄，可躋之于兄上乎！

translations.literal: An elder brother serving a younger—still one may not elevate him; how much less when a younger brother served an elder—can he be elevated above his elder brother!
translations.idiomatic: When an elder brother served a younger, elevation was still forbidden; how much worse when a younger brother served an elder—can the younger be placed above the elder!

sentences.zh: 若以兄弟同昭，則不應出兄置於別廟。

translations.literal: If brothers share the same zhao, then the elder brother should not be removed and placed in a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: If brothers share the same zhao tab, the elder ought not be excluded to a separate shrine.

sentences.zh: 願下群臣博議，遷中宗入廟。」

translations.literal: I ask that the matter be referred to the officials for broad deliberation, and Emperor Zhongzong moved back into the temple."
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to refer this to the officials for full debate and return Emperor Zhongzong to the main temple."

sentences.zh: 事下禮官，太常博士陳貞節、馮宗、蘇獻議，以爲：「七代之廟，不數兄弟。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ritual officials; Grand Masters of Sacrifices Chen Zhenjie, Feng Zong, and Su Xian deliberated, holding that: "In a temple of seven generations, brothers are not counted as separate generations.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the ritual officers; Chen Zhenjie, Feng Zong, and Su Xian of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices argued: "In the seven-generation temple, reigns of brothers are not counted separately.

sentences.zh: 殷代或兄弟四人相繼爲君，若數以爲代，則無祖檷之祭矣。

translations.literal: In the Yin dynasty sometimes four brothers succeeded one another as rulers; if each were counted as a generation, there would be no sacrifice for the ancestral tablet.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yin, four brothers sometimes reigned in succession; if each were counted as a generation, sacrifice to the distant ancestor would be lost.

sentences.zh: 今睿宗之室當亞高宗，故爲中宗特立別廟。

translations.literal: Now Emperor Ruizong's shrine ought to rank below Emperor Gaozong's; therefore a separate temple was specially established for Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong's place properly follows Emperor Gaozong's; that is why a separate shrine was set up for Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 中宗既升新廟，睿宗乃祔高宗，何嘗躋居中宗之上？

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong having been installed in the new temple, Emperor Ruizong was then attached beside Emperor Gaozong—how was he ever elevated above Emperor Zhongzong?
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Zhongzong installed in the new shrine and Emperor Ruizong enshrined beside Emperor Gaozong, how could Ruizong be said to rank above Zhongzong?

sentences.zh: 而平子引躋僖公爲證，誣罔聖朝，漸不可長。」

translations.literal: Yet Pingzi cites elevating Duke Xi as proof—slandering and deceiving the sacred court; such trends must not be allowed to grow."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Pingzi invokes Duke Xi's elevation as precedent—a slander on the sacred court that must not be indulged."

sentences.zh: 時論多是平子，上亦以爲然，故議久不決。

translations.literal: Public opinion mostly sided with Pingzi, and the emperor also thought so; therefore the deliberation long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Most public opinion favored Pingzi, and the emperor agreed; the debate therefore remained unresolved for a long time.

sentences.zh: 蘇獻，頲之從祖兄也，故頲右之。

translations.literal: Su Xian was Su Ting's elder cousin on the paternal side; therefore Su Ting favored his position.
translations.idiomatic: Su Xian was Su Ting's elder cousin, which is why Su Ting sided with him.

sentences.zh: 卒從禮官議。

translations.literal: In the end they followed the ritual officers' opinion.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the court followed the ritual officers' view.

sentences.zh: 平子論之不巳，謫爲康州都城尉。

translations.literal: Pingzi, not ceasing his argument, was demoted to capital-district warden of Kang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because Pingzi would not cease arguing, he was exiled to serve as warden of Kangzhou's capital district.

sentences.zh: 新廟成。

translations.literal: The new temple was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The new shrine was completed.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，神主祔廟。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day, the spirit tablets were installed in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day, the spirit tablets were enshrined.

sentences.zh: 上命宋璟、蘇頲爲諸皇子制名及國邑之號，又令別制一佳名及佳號進之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Song Jing and Su Ting to devise names for the princes and designations for their fiefs, and also ordered them separately to devise one fine name and fine designation to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged Song Jing and Su Ting with naming the princes and designating their fiefs, and also asked them to submit a separate list of especially fine names and titles.

sentences.zh: 璟等上言：「七子均養，著於《國風》。

translations.literal: Jing and the others submitted: "The equal nurturing of seven sons is recorded in the Guofeng.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and his colleagues submitted: "The Book of Songs' Guofeng praises a mother who nurtures seven sons alike.

sentences.zh: 今臣等所制名號各三十餘，輒混同以進，以彰陛下覆燾無偏之德。」

translations.literal: Now the names and designations we have devised number more than thirty each; we venture to submit them mixed together, to display Your Majesty's virtue of covering and nurturing without partiality."
translations.idiomatic: We have drawn up more than thirty names and titles each, and submit them as a single combined list to reflect Your Majesty's impartial, sheltering virtue."

sentences.zh: 上甚善之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was much pleased.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙申，契丹王李失活入朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the bingshen day, Khitan king Li Shihuo entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the bingshen day, Li Shihuo, king of the Khitan, came to court.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬午，以東平王外孫楊氏爲永樂公主，妻之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the renwu day, Yang, granddaughter of the Prince of Dongping, was made Princess Yongle and given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the renwu day, Lady Yang, granddaughter of the Prince of Dongping, was ennobled as Princess Yongle and given to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 秘書監馬懷素奏：「省中書散亂訛缺，請選學術之士二十人整經校補。」

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Library Ma Huaisu memorialized: "The books in the secretariat are in disorder with errors and omissions; I ask that twenty men of scholarly learning be selected to put the classics in order, collate, and supplement them."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huaisu, director of the Imperial Library, memorialized: "The palace library's texts are disordered and defective; please select twenty scholars to collate and restore the classics."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] consented.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 於是搜訪逸書，選吏繕寫，命國子博士尹知章、桑泉尉韋述等二十人同刊正，以左散騎常侍褚無量爲之使，於乾元殿前編校群書。

translations.literal: Thereupon lost books were sought out, clerks were chosen to copy them, and twenty men including National University Erudite Yin Zhizhang and Sangquan district warden Wei Shu were ordered jointly to collate and correct them; Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse Chu Wuliang was made their commissioner, and at the front of the Qianyuan Hall they compiled and collated the collected books.
translations.idiomatic: Lost texts were then sought out, clerks were assigned to copy them, and twenty scholars—including National University erudite Yin Zhizhang and Sangquan district warden Wei Shu—were put to collating them under Chu Wuliang, left regular attendant of the Palace Horse, who supervised the work before the Qianyuan Hall.
